items.text:
US too focused on Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough, Zelensky tells BBC
- Published
Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, saying that delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and complaining that the US is not pushing Russia hard enough during peace talks.
In an interview with the BBC at his office in central Kyiv, Ukraine's president also said it was "very strange" that Donald Trump had posted a picture of himself embracing Vladimir Putin as "my friend".
"Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English.
"He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, suggesting it was like hugging Adolf Hitler during WWII.
Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States.
Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv.
The latest round of peace talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress: "The more we know, the more problems", is how Zelensky described it.
He said talks were expected to resume in December.
On Thursday, Donald Trump posted on his Truth Social platform that at his own summit with Putin in China last week he had urged Russia to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe" and said he believed a peace deal with Ukraine was "a strong possibility".
But from its public statements, Russia appears to have regressed to its initial, hardline negotiating positions – on everything.
And Zelensky revealed that it wasn't clear whether European negotiators would be at the table, as the US envoys had announced.
The Kremlin appears to be resisting.
- Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say 
  - Published6 days ago
- Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend 
  - Published5 days ago
Ukraine urgently needs the talks to move forward and bring five exhausting years of Russia's full-scale invasion to an end.
Russian strikes across the country have been growing more frequent and more deadly: the number of civilians being killed is at an all-time high.
So Zelensky called for "real helpful allies, who can push Russia" to achieve results and urged the US to live up to its reputation as a strong country with "power and respect".
"When you try to be very neutral with the aggressor... it means you support victims and you support also aggressor. It's not right," he said.
The US argues that it is neutral: in the complex search for a peace deal between the two sides that can hold.
In the meantime, Kyiv is struggling to defend its skies.
The air alerts, day and night, are now a draining feature of everyday life. As Russian ballistic missiles target power stations and bridges, jet-powered drones are launched daily at central Kyiv and other big cities.
Ukraine launches hundreds of drones at targets in Russia in response.
Zelensky said the military here are now able to destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones, a statistic he said was improving.
But there is a "very, very big" deficit of interceptors to stop ballistic missiles and he said the Amercians were delaying deliveries of its Patriot systems.
"It's a pity they made a focus on Middle East and they help them more… It's a pity. We have huge questions with this," Zelensky said.
"The deficit of these missiles - that is people's lives."
He also confirmed that the US satellite communications system, Starlink – and its military version, Starshield – were still being restricted in occupied areas of Ukraine.
Ukrainian drone units have described their problems to the BBC, as their interceptor drones can no longer catch up with Russian Shaheds. It means those weapons then fly deeper into Ukraine, unhindered.
So whose decision was that?
"Technically SpaceX, politically - I don't know, I really don't know," Zelensky replied. "It's like... ping pong. We are asking one side, they say it's the other."
Tough winter
Ukraine's own long-range strikes against Russian targets have increased in recent weeks, including oil refineries and ships carrying weapons or fuel.
On Thursday, Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said an attack that sank a Russian warship docked in eastern Libya this week risked spreading war to the Mediterranean, which was unacceptable.
Zelensky defended the strikes, calling the warship Merkury an "absolutely fair goal".
He accepted that such strikes were "very dangerous" but said Ukraine's forces "never attack" without coordinating with its partners.
He declined to be more specific.
But he acknowledged that Ukraine was bracing for a difficult and dangerous winter.
Recent strikes on Kyiv have targeted bridges over the vast river Dnipro, apparently trying to cut the city in two.
Some residents have already left town for the winter and businesses closed, as power cuts and strikes on logistics networks have pushed operating costs unmanageably high.
They've also plunged much of the city into darkness.
"[Russia] wants us to run away, of course," Zelensky said.
"People can go, but we will try to defend our capital in any way. We need our capital. Without a capital, you don't have a country."

- Published
Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after staging a 10-man fightback to join a select band of teams to win their first five European games.
The Cherries trailed 1-0 to Iago Aspas' goal at Celta Vigo,
items.text:
Bournemouth 'allowed to dream' as fans book Europa League final hotels
- Published
Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after staging a 10-man fightback to join a select band of teams to win their first five European games.
The Cherries trailed 1-0 to Iago Aspas' goal at Celta Vigo, and then went down to 10 men midway through the first half when Bafode Diakite was sent off.
But second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan gave the Cherries a 10th consecutive win in all competitions, extending their club record run.
Bournemouth are only the third side to win each of their first five European matches (excluding qualifiers and including the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup), after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73.
They top this season's table as the only club to win five out of five - and are closing in on a top-eight spot, which would mean they skip a play-off round and go straight into the last 16.
Some fans have told the BBC they have already booked hotels in Frankfurt for the final on 26 May.
As supporters sang about reaching that game, midfielder Alex Scott was asked for his thoughts on TNT Sports.
"Of course that's our dream. When you grow up wanting to be a footballer you dream of winning trophies," Scott said.
"Where this club has come from to where it is now, full credit to everyone who has built it.
"For players, it's a dream to be on the pitch playing for this club. We have still got wins to get to qualify into the top eight, and from there all focus is on pushing forward and hopefully we can go on and win it."
'We were just relentless'
The Cherries are in unprecedented times, with their biggest trophy to date being when they won the second-tier Championship in 2014-15.
In terms of cups, they won the 1983–84 Associate Members' Cup - which later became the EFL Trophy.
Head coach Marco Rose, who replaced Andoni Iraola in the summer, said: "It's always allowed to dream.
"If you get a competition like this you want to achieve the best possible thing. We know it's far away to go. Many games. Now it's about getting into the top eight to avoid more games and then we can see step by step."
As well as just winning their games, Bournemouth are firing in the goals. They have netted at least twice in each match during this 10-game winning run.
And they are the first side to score at least twice in each of their first five matches in Europe since Queens Park Rangers in 1976.
The win on Thursday was made even more impressive by the fact they contested 75% of the game with 10 men.
It came days after Manchester United seemed to implode after an early red card against Liverpool, losing 4-0.
Former England manager Glenn Hoddle said on TNT: "They have deserved this result. They've played beautifully with 10 men - probably as good as I've seen a team play defensively and with the ball.
"I've not seen a team go down to 10 men for so long and dictate a game and deserve to win the game. They were absolutely brilliant."
Cherries boss Rose told BBC Radio Solent: "What a team, what a spirit, what an energy.
"I said to Ty [Tyler Adams] sometimes it's not about tactics and formations and stuff like this. [David] Brooks did a great job when we got one player less - he played right defender like he played it for 10 years. We changed in the right moment. Everyone did his job on a really high level.
"We were just relentless and we never stopped to believe in this win and that's why big, big, big congratulations to the team.
"You feel if you're one player down that it's a difficult night, but to handle a difficult night like this, it just shows the character of the team and of the whole group."
The coach's belief in what they are doing filters through to the players.
Amine Adli, who set up the equaliser, told the BBC: "At half-time, everyone still believed we can turn the game in our way and this is what happened.
"Everyone was like 'guys we can make it, we have to believe. If we score the game can change.'"
Earlier this month, the attacking midfielder said he saw a lot of similarities to the Bayer Leverkusen team he was part of in 2023-24.
That is not a bad comparison, considering they went unbeaten to win the domestic double, as well as reaching the Europa League final.
So who can blame the Cherries for dreaming?

items.title: Reinildo error extends Sunderland woe as Jagiellonia grab Europa League draw
items.summary:
Jagiellonia Bialystok’s head coach, Adrian Siemieniec claimed this trip to Wearside to face Premier League opposition represented one of the biggest highlights of a career that has already seen him celebrate a Polish title.
His players did everything to guarantee it was not an anticlimax as they del
items.text:
Jagiellonia Bialystok’s head coach, Adrian Siemieniec claimed this trip to Wearside to face Premier League opposition represented one of the biggest highlights of a career that has already seen him celebrate a Polish title.
His players did everything to guarantee it was not an anticlimax as they delighted in highlighting Sunderland’s struggles in front of goal courtesy of some intelligent defending. Along the way they also responded to falling behind with an almost immediate equaliser and forced Robin Roefs into the evening’s more taxing saves.
The city of Bialystok lies in eastern Poland, close to the Belarusian and Lithuanian borders but the arduous journey to north-east England was not responsible for the lack of Jagiellonia fans inside the Stadium of Light.
Instead visiting supporters were banned from making the trip by Uefa as punishment for misbehaviour at Levski Sofia earlier this season. Their absence contributed to a strangely flat atmosphere on a brutally cold Wearside night. Although a reasonably strong Sunderland starting XI were largely dominant they struggled to undo Jagiellonia’s indefatigable defence.
Granted Enzo Le Fée contributed some lovely touches and often looked the best player on the pitch but Régis Le Bris’s playmaker needed support and it seemed in scant supply. When Le Fée cued up Nilson Angulo a goal seemed inevitable but a splendid visiting block served as a reminder that Jagiellonia appeared determined to play in the spirit of their founders – soldiers from the 42nd infantry regiment of the Polish army.
At least Malick Fofana’s confidence should have been boosted by a superbly calibrated left foot shot that forced a stellar save from Slawomir Abramowicz. The Belgium winger has struggled since arriving from Lyon in a £30m summer deadline day move but here was a hint – albeit fairly isolated – of the potential that led Sunderland to engage in an extraordinary transfer tug of war with Crystal Palace before eventually winning his signature.
Although Robin Roefs was forced into just one significant first-half save – to repel Kajetan Szmyt’s free-kick – Omar Alderete’s struggles this season continued in the shape of an error-strewn performance. In mitigation perhaps the centre-half – excellent last season – was struggling with an injury as, shortly before half-time, he signalled to the bench that he needed to come off and was replaced by Luke O’Nien.
Le Bris introduced two more new faces at the outset of the second period as, with Sunday’s all important home Premier League game with Tottenham looming, he offered Noah Sadiki and Trai Hume rests, sending Jules Ahoka and Thomas Meunier on in their place. The newcomers were soon celebrating. When Le Fée crossed incisively from the right Timur Tutierov was just onside and the young Ukrainian striker delighted in heading Sunderland in front from point black range.
That lead did not last long. Errors on the part of Ahoka and then, most significantly, Reinildo’s panicked, failed, attempted back pass left Kamil Jozwiak free to round Roefs and sweep an imperious equalising shot into the back of the net.
The need to keep Le Fée’s legs reasonably fresh for Spurs saw the Frenchman replaced by Chemsdine Talbi. By then Roefs had made an excellent save to deny Jozwiak a second goal after another mistake from the immensely promising yet deeply inexperienced Ahoka and the simmering disgruntlement of Sunderland fans was becoming audible.
When visiting substitute Jesús Imaz subsequently directed an extremely presentable chance straight at Roefs there was a sense calamity had been averted. Even so, A smattering of boos greeted the final whistle as a frowning Le Bris’s hopes of avoiding the playoffs and qualifying automatically for the knockout phase receded.

items.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
items.summary: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s came 17 minutes from time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory was turn
items.text:
Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s came 17 minutes from time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory was turned on its head after Jon Martin was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser.
The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none. The Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step despite Yéremy Pino’s missed penalty in injury time after the outstanding Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory.
Frank had urged the Palace supporters ensure the atmosphere was “through the roof” for his home debut and he immediately made a beeline for the Holmesdale Road End after emerging from the tunnel. Almost all of his squad – including the two substitute goalkeepers – had spent a substantial part of the warm-up practising defending set pieces so there was no doubt where the priorities lay. But the Palace manager didn’t look amused when Mamadou Sarr was inches away from connecting with a free-kick in the second minute as the visitors served warning of the threat they posed.
Sociedad have struggled in this competition despite a promising start to their La Liga campaign and it was a surprise to see Pellegrino Matarazzo match Frank’s 4-4-2 formation in what felt like something of a throwback to the mid 1990s. With Adam Wharton suspended after his red card against Hoffenheim, Palace found it very difficult to escape their press as Mateta and Eddie Nketiah were forced to feed off whatever scraps that came their way.
Ben Chilwell looked unsettled by the pace of Héctor Fort, the former Barcelona right-back, and Sociedad began to target the former England defender’s left flank. Mikel Oyarzabal should have done much better when he was picked out by the lively Arsen Zakharyan.
Not for the first time, Palace had Henderson to thank for keeping the scores level when Zakharyan was given far too much time and space by Chilwell. The Russian picked out Goncalo Guedes and his shot was parried away to safety. The former Wolves forward tried his luck again soon after and once more Henderson was equal to his effort. The Palace captain could not hide his emotions as he rightly questioned why their opponents were being afforded so much space. Mateta had to wait until the final minute of the first half for a sighter and the France striker could only nod over from a long Chris Richards throw.
Henderson was called into action twice inside the opening six minutes of the second half as Sociedad smelled blood. Oyarzabal should have rounded off a lightning-quick break downfield but could only shoot straight at the England goalkeeper before Jon Gorrotxategi was denied from the edge of the area. With his side struggling to gain a foothold, Frank abandoned his experiment with Nketiah and brought on Dwight McNeil to try to give Chilwell a helping hand. Yet it was down Palace’s left flank that Sociedad finally found the breakthrough when Sarr touched home Job Ochieng’s cros
To their credit, Palace’s response was immediate. Disasi won a header from another long throw and Martin hauled down Mateta as he was about to score, earning a second yellow card. Mateta dispatched the spot kick with aplomb and only a desperate goalline clearance from Sarr denied Kamada. Frank went for broke by throwing on Jorgen Strand Larsen and his gamble paid off when the Norway striker’s attempted overhead kick presented McNeil with the easiest of opportunities to lift the gloom in these parts.

The New York Times has reported that the United States Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) may have
items.text:
Report: CIA tortured more people with waterboarding than US agency admitted
A New York Times report lends credence to the long-held belief that the torture method was more widely used than acknowledged.
The New York Times has reported that the United States Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) may have waterboarded more people than it previously admitted.
Wednesday’s report comes after the newspaper filed a lawsuit to obtain material gathered by special prosecutor John Durham, who was appointed in 2008 to investigate the CIA’s activities.
Durham’s probe ended without any criminal charges. But The New York Times obtained partially redacted documents from his investigation, including a summary of a 2012 interview with an interpreter who described a previously unconfirmed act of waterboarding.
The account sheds new light on one of the most infamous methods of torture utilised by the intelligence agency after the attacks on September 11, 2001.
Waterboarding involves restraining a person and pouring water on their face through a cloth, to mimic the experience of drowning.
The CIA called the practice an “enhanced interrogation technique”. As part of the US’s so-called “war on terror”, the agency sent suspects to overseas prisons, known as black sites, where they would be tortured in secret, including through waterboarding.
While the practice was shielded from scrutiny for years, a 2009 executive order eventually barred continued waterboarding. Congress has likewise passed restrictions.
But rights groups have long suspected that such abuses were much more widespread than the CIA admitted. The agency had previously acknowledged waterboarding three detainees.
According to the documents The New York Times received, a contract translator who worked with the CIA observed an additional case of waterboarding.
While the documents do not specify where the translator worked, the newspaper said it determined that the location was likely a black site outside of Bagram Air Force Base on the outskirts of Kabul, Afghanistan.
The translator, The New York Times explained, referenced a detainee death that matched a facility known as Detention Site Cobalt or the “Salt Pit”, which became infamous for abusive conditions.
In an interview with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the translator stated that he had seen a man referred to as “Bashir” facing the torture practice.
He described Bahir as “lying on the board with the head of the board tilted downward into the water”.
“There were approximately three to four people ‘doing this,’” the document said, summarising the translator’s statements.
The FBI summary explains that the translator “saw the incident in passing but did not participate himself”. The incident allegedly took place in a hallway.
The CIA did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment by the time of this article’s publication.
The agency has also not acknowledged waterboarding detainees at any site in Afghanistan. The three detainees it has acknowledged torturing were held at black sites in Thailand and Poland.
One was Abu Zubaydah, the first detainee the CIA held in a black-site prison, located in Thailand. The US government for years falsely depicted him as one of the highest-ranking members of al-Qaeda, a group of which he was not a member, according to US intelligence reports.
A 2014 report on the CIA torture programme by the Senate Intelligence Committee found that Zubaydah was waterboarded 83 times, sometimes as a means of helping instruct torture methods.
Another was Khalid Shaikh Mohammed, accused of being the architect of the September 11 attacks.
The third was Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, who is accused of helping plan al-Qaeda’s 2000 bombing of a Navy destroyer, the USS Cole.
All three are currently being held in the Guantanamo Bay military prison in Cuba.

Torreense 1-2 Celtic: Camilo Duran comes off bench to score late winner and keep Hoops' Europa League hopes alive
Report from the Europa League clash between Torreense and Celtic at Campo Manuel Marques; Javi Vazquez' own-goal put Celtic in front; Dany Jean levelled before the break; substitute Camilo Duran headed in a late winner for the Hoops; Martin O'Neill's side are up to 25th
Thursday 26 November 2026 22:55, UK
Camilo Duran came off the bench to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive with a vital win against Torreense.
The Colombian striker peeled away to the back post to meet a cross from fellow substitute James Forrest, guiding a downward header into the net in the 85th minute.
Duran's 15th goal of the season secured a 2-1 victory over the Portuguese second-tier side and moved Celtic on to six points in the Europa League. His latest decisive contribution follows a match-winning double off the bench in the Hoops' comeback victory over Besiktas last time out.
- Teams | Stats | Europa League fixtures and results
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Celtic games with no contract📺
Celtic took the lead in the ninth minute when Javi Vazquez turned Jota's cross into his own net, with Yang Hyun-jun lurking behind him.
However, the Portuguese Cup winners hit back 10 minutes later after some hesitant defending from the visitors. Alex Alfaro rattled the crossbar with a 22-yard effort, but neither Kieran Tierney nor Colby Donovan could deal with the resulting loose balls, allowing Haiti international Dany Jean to volley home the equaliser.
Celtic dominated possession after the break but struggled to create clear-cut opportunities until Duran's late intervention secured all three points.
The Hoops' attention now turns to Hearts on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, as they look to remain top of the Scottish Premiership.
Their next Europa League match is away to Omonia Nicosia on December 10.
Key moments from Campo Manuel Marques
2: CLOSE! Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain sends in a corner, it's flicked on by Liam Scales but Hyun-jun Yang can't knock the ball in before it's cleared.
9: GOAL CELTIC! Javi Vazquez tries to clear Jota's cross but turns it into his own net.
19: GOAL TORREENSE! Alex Alfaro's effort rattles the underside of the bar, Celtic fail to make a clearance and Dany Jean fires in the equaliser.
33: SAVE! Jota's powerful strike is pushed over the bar by Adriel.
36: OFF THE LINE! More awful defending from Celtic, but Liam Scales manages to head the ball clear.
47: SAVE! Jota tries to chip the ball over the goalkeeper but he manages to pluck the ball out of the air.
53: BLOCK! Jota is continuing to cause problems for the hosts as he sends in a cross for Kieran Tierney, which is headed behind.
61: CLOSE! Jean looks to squeeze in a shot at the near post, but it's just wide.
69: CHANCE! A misplaced pass from Oliver Sorensen lets Musa Drammeh get a shot away. Thankfully for Celtic it's wide.
70: LET OFF FOR CELTIC! Trouble at the back again gives Drammeh space to get a shot away, but the former Hearts striker is inches wide.
84: GOAL CELTIC! Camilo Duran rises at the back post to head in James Forrest's cross. Celtic are back ahead.
O'Neill: 'From an almost impossible position, we have hope'
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill on TNT Sports:
"I'm just delighted to have won, it keeps us going if nothing else. We've got six points on the board and we've still a couple of games to go.
"From an almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we've given ourselves some hope.
"Three points tonight were of vital importance. There's lots we can still do to improve our game."
Asked about Camilo Duran, he added: "He's just a magnificent footballer.
"15 goals and we're not into December, he's been flying. He's a terrific player, and that's two games he's come up big for us."
Jota 'enjoying life' as he returns to best
Celtic winger Jota speaking to TNT Sports after his first European appearance for almost two years:
"It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible.
"Right now, it's all about enjoying life. No expectations, just be professional and having the responsibility of being a Celtic player.
"It wasn't easy. I think we just had to stick with our plan and in the end it worked out, that's the most important thing.
"We must believe [Celtic can qualify]. Every game is a different battle, we know what to do."

Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad: Thomas Frank earns first win as Eagles boss with Europa League comeback victory
Match report as Thomas Frank earns his first win as Crystal Palace manager; Mamadou Sarr gave Real Sociedad the lead after a dominant opening hour; Jon Martin was sent off and Jean-Philippe Mateta scored from the penalty spot to level; Dwight McNeill score the winner
Thursday 26 November 2026 22:13, UK
Thomas Frank earned his first win as Crystal Palace manager, coming from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.
The Dane lost his opening game to Coventry at the weekend, but saw the heart and fight he will need from his side as they picked up their second win in the competition this season.
For 70 minutes, Sociedad dominated at Selhurst Park, with Dean Henderson needed to make a string of saves. They finally made the breakthrough when Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr tapped home from Job Ochieng's cross.
- Teams | Stats | Europa League fixtures and results
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
But the game turned out of nowhere as Crystal Palace were awarded a penalty and Jon Martin was sent off. He picked up a second yellow card for holding Jean-Philippe Mateta round the middle, with the striker expertly dispatching the spot kick to level for the Eagles.
The confidence surged in the hosts - backed by the famous atmosphere at Selhurst Park - and it was a well-worked second that put them ahead.
Yeremy Pino's cross was cleared to Jorgen Strand Larsen at the back post, who hit an overhead kick. It wasn't on target, but it did bobble into the six-yard box for the incoming Dwight McNeill, who slid to poke home.
Crystal Palace could have wrapped up the points in a topsy-turvy end after they were awarded another penalty. Carlos Soler was penalised for handball, but Pino's effort was well-saved by Unai Marrero.
The win catapults Crystal Palace into 12th place in the league phase table, just two from the top eight, and gives them a huge boost ahead of another key clash against Hull on Super Sunday. Real Sociedad have slid down into 27th.

You can follow developments from the EU summit taking place on Thursday 26th and Friday 27th November below:
EU leaders to meet later tonight, Merz says
Contrary to earlier expectations, European Union leaders weren't quite done for the day, even if it was well past 2200 local time.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said that rather than meet again as scheduled on Friday, leaders would hold a final round of discussions around midnight and end the summit.
Thank you for following our coverage
Thank you for reading along with our coverage of the Euro Summit on Thursday.
We will be back tomorrow to bring you the latest from the second day.
Until then, you can watch DW's analysis of the event:
Hungary's Magyar sees 'virtually zero chance' of reaching a deal on Thursday
Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar has said the chances of reaching an agreement on Thursday are "virtually zero."
Leaders of the European Union are gathered today in Brussels to agree on the bloc's budget proposal for 2028 to 2034.
In an X post, Magyar said he outlined "Hungary’s priorities and the red lines" to the other member states.
"Having heard the completely opposing positions around the table, I would put the chances of reaching an agreement today at virtually zero," he wrote.
He also said "an agreement around Christmas looks unlikely" as well.
Pedro Sanchez welcomes nomination of Hernandez de Cos as new ECB chief
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez celebrated "a Spain that leads in Europe like never before," after the nomination of Pablo Hernandez de Cos as the next European Central Bank (ECB) chief.
Hernandez de Cos is set to become the new ECB head as the European Union (EU) leaders are gathered in Brussels for the Euro Summit.
Sanchez welcomed the news in a post on X, pointing out that the top EU positions held by Spanish officials Teresa Ribera, the European Commission's First Executive Vice-President, and Nadia Calvino, head of the European Investment Bank.
"In short, Spain leads in Europe like never before," he wrote.
Pablo Hernandez de Cos is set to become the new European Central Bank chief — reports
Spanish candidate Pablo Hernandez de Cos will become the next president of the European Central Bank (ECB), after being endorsed by the majority ‌of eurozone countries, news agencies reported.
As the leaders gather for the Euro Summit, the Financial Times first reported that de Cos will be the next ECB chief, citing people familiar with the matter. This was confirmed by Reuters and AFP, citing EU diplomat sources.
The decision came after the Netherlands said it would support the Spaniard as a consensus candidate.
Christine Lagarde has been president since November 2019 but has announced her intention to step down on February 7, 2027.
De Cos was up against Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot for the presidency, while France's Laurence Boone and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier have been nominated for the ECB's two other top jobs.
Russia says EU budget plans would prolong war in Ukraine
Russia has criticized the European Union's proposed seven-year budget, accusing the bloc of seeking to prolong the war in Ukraine.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the EU's plans to allocate money for Ukraine in its budget would make Kyiv "less inclined toward a peace process and more determined to continue the war."
Peskov said the result would be more military spending, leaving less for governments to spend on school, hospitals and social facilities.
"This is not money for peace," Peskov said.
Support for Ukraine is among the key areas of discussion in the 2028-2034 budget which includes up to €100 billion for Ukraine, however diplomats say this figure falls well short of Kyiv's needs.
EU 'light-years' from budget deal, Italy PM Meloni says
Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has added her voice to those warning that European leaders have their work cut out for them when it comes to agreeing on a multi-year budget proposal.
"We're light-years ‌away from a ‌solution," Meloni told reporters ahead of the EU summit in Brussels.
"We are not willing to sign off on a budget under which ‌we would have to give more to receive less," she added.
Earlier, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the budget was "still too high" and that members states needed to be able to afford the full cost without taking on new debt.
Last week, European Council President Antonio Costa presented a new compromise proposal of €1.78 trillion ($1.95 trillion), around €204 billion lower than the initial proposal by the European Commission.
Analysis: The battle for Europe's future behind closed doors
Every seven years, European leaders gather in Brussels for what is arguably the most consequential negotiation cycle in the European Union. As German Chancellor Friedrich Merz put it upon arrival, it is about "the future of the European Union."
This is not a typical EU summit. The leaders of the 27 member states are confronting a question that will shape all angles of EU politics for years to come: How much money should the EU have, who should pay for it, and what should it be spent on?
It is the essence of EU summit diplomacy: a painstaking exercise in give-and-take, bargaining and compromise.
The European Commission laid down the opening bid over the summer. The proposal was ambitious. Brussels wants an EU budget that reflects a rapidly-changing world: more spending on defence, innovation, research, digital technologies and competitiveness. Fury vs Joshua undercard: Martin Bakole insists late-notice Deontay Wilder fight won't be like Joseph Parker loss
In his first interview since agreeing to step in to fight Deontay Wilder, Martin Bakole explains his decision and why he believes this late-notice assignment will be very different from
items.text:
Fury vs Joshua undercard: Martin Bakole insists late-notice Deontay Wilder fight won't be like Joseph Parker loss
In his first interview since agreeing to step in to fight Deontay Wilder, Martin Bakole explains his decision and why he believes this late-notice assignment will be very different from when he flew in to fight Joseph Parker; Bakole says victory will lead him to a world title shot
Thursday 26 November 2026 22:06, UK
Martin Bakole explained his decision to step in as a replacement opponent for Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard next month.
After Jai Opetaia withdrew from his December 11 bout with former heavyweight world champion Wilder, Bakole came in to take his place on the Principality Stadium bill.
He insists it is a very different scenario to his short-notice assignment against Joseph Parker last year.
Bakole came in to box Parker for the WBO Interim title, landing in Riyadh just a day before the fight. Parker promptly put him down heavily and stopped him in their second round.
For this fight with Wilder though he's had more warning. He was training in Las Vegas to box on the same bill, albeit originally for a much lower-level opponent.
"When I heard Wilder doesn't have an opponent, his opponent cancelled, they proposed me and I said why not? I'm ready to give a big fight," Bakole told Sky Sports. "Why not jump from a comeback fight to a big fight?
"I was surprised they mentioned my name and I said yes," he added. "I'm ready to come back again because I want to take over now the heavyweight division.
"I don't see Deontay beating me. He doesn't have the strength I have.
"I don't see any danger because I like danger, I like to impose myself.
"I'm ready and prepared for him."
That wasn't the case for Parker when he took that fight. "I was out in the Congo on holiday, I jumped in," Bakole said.
"In that fight I was giving Joseph Parker a hard time in the first round but because I was not fit and my head was not moving, he landed a punch. But I don't regret that fight. It's just part of my story.
"That was something to save the card."
While Bakole has been training in Las Vegas, he will still have long-time coach Billy Nelson in his corner for the fight.
"I came here to learn something new. I was getting ready for everyone," Bakole said. "Everything has changed [with his preparation], conditioning, nutrition."
He believes victory over Wilder will lead him to a world title shot next year.
"Of course," Bakole said. "That's why I wanted to change everything because I know next year, with my team, with His Excellency's [Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh] help, I will get a world title next year."

items.title: Bears stun Lions with TD in final seconds of NFL Thanksgiving epic
items.summary:
NFL: Chicago Bears stun Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving with game-winning touchdown in final three seconds
Detroit Lions lead for 53 minutes and 31 seconds, stretching their advantage to 11 points midway through final quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs' third TD from 70 yards out; Rome Odunze scores twice, in
items.text:
NFL: Chicago Bears stun Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving with game-winning touchdown in final three seconds
Detroit Lions lead for 53 minutes and 31 seconds, stretching their advantage to 11 points midway through final quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs' third TD from 70 yards out; Rome Odunze scores twice, including game-winner, to clinch Chicago Bears comeback that secures top spot in NFC North
Thursday 26 November 2026 22:08, UK
The Chicago Bears scored the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds remaining to secure a stunning 39-35 comeback win over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving and claim first place in the NFC North.
Rome Odunze's second TD - a sensational toe-tap grab in the back of the end zone - clinched the victory and deny Detroit, who had led by 11 earlier in the fourth quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs ran in his third score of the game from 70 yards out.
Chicago's lead secured right at the death was the first lead change in a game they've been involved with since they trailed the Carolina Panthers 7-0 in the first quarter of their opening game of the season. They had trailed the Lions for 53 minutes and 31 seconds of this match.
- How to watch NFL Thanksgiving week live on Sky Sports
- Jay-Z picks himself to headline Super Bowl half-time show
- Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW
The Bears' dramatic win nudges them into solo first in the fiercely-fought NFC North, at 9-2 on the season, while the Lions drop to 8-3 with a first loss in seven.
It also improves Chicago's record in the division to 1-2, with Detroit now 2-1, which could prove crucial should any potential playoff tiebreakers be necessary to separate the two teams - who meet again on the penultimate week of the season - or the Minnesota Vikings (7-3) and Green Bay Packers (6-5).
The game was initially slow to ignite, with only a Lions field goal to show from the first quarter, before Gibbs' first score to start the second lit the blue touchpaper.
The Lions continued to lead thereafter, until the Bears came roaring back in the final quarter. Caleb Williams firstly located Odunze deep down the field for a 41-yard TD, the QB ran in the resulting two-point play to cut the score to three, before Jared Goff threw an interception on the next series.
Chicago turned the ball over on downs, failing to convert on 4th and 3 just inside Detroit territory, but they got the ball back with just over two minutes to go, and this time marched down the field before Williams linked up with Odunze again for the game winner with seconds remaining.
Williams finished with 345 yards passing and those two scoring strikes to Odunze, while Bears running back D'Andre Swift had 162 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. Gibbs had 20 carries for a massive 205 yards and three TDs for the Lions but it didn't prove to be enough.
Stats leaders
Bears:
- Passing: Caleb Williams, 30/44, 345 yards, 2 TDs
- Rushing: D'Andre Swift, 9 carries, 65 yards, 1 TD
- Receiving: D'Andre Swift, 7 catches, 97 yards
- Rome Odunze, 6 catches, 87 yards, 2 TDs
Lions:
- Passing: Jared Goff, 25/36, 313 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT
- Rushing: Jahmyr Gibbs, 21 carries, 205 yards, 3 TDs
- Receiving: Amon-Ra St. Brown, 7 catches, 146 yards
How the Bears roared back on Thanksgiving
After the Lions' first quarter field goal, they failed to add further points on the back of a Colston Loveland fumble, but they would find the end zone early in the second - Gibbs from down at the goal line - as the Bears offense was slow to fire.
Chicago finally sparked into life in the second and tied the game up at 10-10 with the first of two Kyle Monangai scores.
Detroit were back in front by the half, up 19-10, after a bizarre sequence saw them first awarded a safety as a Bears player deliberately batted a fumbled football out of the end zone, before Goff found Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard TD.
A second Gibbs touchdown was sandwiched in between scores for Monangai and Swift in the third quarter, while Jake Bates' second field goal put the Lions 29-24 up early in the fourth.
Gibbs only added to that advantage as he completed his hat-trick of TDs with the best of the bunch, breaking loose from 70 yards out but the game was far from over, with Willams and Odunze answering back almost immediately.
After Chicago failed to capitalise on Goff's interception, Detroit missed the chance to ice the game when opting against a 50-yard field goal try as they went for it on 4th and 4 from the Bears 33-yard-line.
Stopped short, Chicago got the ball back to pave the way for Williams and Odunze's dramatic, game-winning connection in the closing seconds.

The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign
items.text:
Two Italians killed in strike in Kuwait, as Iran denies responsibility
- Published
Two Italian nationals have died following a strike on a facility in Kuwait which both countries have blamed on Iran.
The pair were technicians working for German arms manufacturing company Rheinmetall, Italy's foreign ministry said.
Iran has denied responsibility for the attack, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying the incident looked "suspicious" and that Tehran would work with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the cause".
Kuwait's defence ministry said earlier that four people - the two Italians, a Kuwaiti national and Pakistani national - had been injured from falling shrapnel after a number of drones from Iran were detected and intercepted.
It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled overnight Iranian drone attacks on an airbase which hosts US forces - the first strikes in more than two months on the country.
Recent exchanges of fire between the US and Iran, and a deadlock in negotiations, have raised fears of a major escalation in the war.
The conflict began when US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, with Iran retaliating by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
On Thursday, Araghchi said he had expressed condolences over the deaths in calls with his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts and that the incident looked like a "precooked recipe for war", without expanding further.
Earlier, the country's armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi said "no military or offensive operations have been conducted" by Iran.
Kuwait's Army said the latest attack was on a "vital site in the country" and was the result of "heinous Iranian aggression", while confirming the deaths of the two Italian nationals.
Italy's foreign minister was quoted by Italian media as saying that investigations showed that the drone used in the attack was manufactured in Iran and that Iranian proxies were known to carry out attacks in the region.
The two Italian nationals were working at an air defence detection station and performing maintenance work on systems used by the Kuwaiti Armed Forces, according to Italian press agency Ansa, citing Italy's foreign ministry.
Italian media outlets have named the two individuals. One of the men was reported to be 36, while the other was 65 and nearing retirement.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wrote on X: "On my own behalf and on behalf of the government, I express my deepest sympathy and offer my heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.
"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on social media: "We must step up pressure on Iran to end these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf.
"Today's events are a further reminder that security in the Gulf is a security issue for us all."

items.title: Iranian monarchists disrupt Paris event, highlighting bitter diaspora divide
items.summary:
Iranian monarchists disrupt Paris event, highlighting bitter diaspora divide
A Paris event on Iranian women's rights attended by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was disrupted when diaspora supporters of Reza Pahlavi, the US-based son of Iran's deposed shah, taunted left-leaning opponents of
items.text:
Iranian monarchists disrupt Paris event, highlighting bitter diaspora divide
A Paris event on Iranian women's rights attended by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was disrupted when diaspora supporters of Reza Pahlavi, the US-based son of Iran's deposed shah, taunted left-leaning opponents of Iran's Islamic regime. The chaos underscored the bitter divides in the Iranian diaspora as the Iran war enters its tenth month.
Activists backing Iran's ousted monarchy disrupted an event in Paris aiming to amplify the voices of Iranian women, prompting a bitter dispute Thursday between supporters of the deposed shah and left-wing opponents of the Islamic republic.
Analysts said the incident late Wednesday at the Arab World Institute (IMA) highlighted the deep divisions between diaspora opponents of Iran's clerical leadership, even after a wave of protests earlier this year.
The event, attended by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, was meant to project the voices of women inside Iran to mark the international day to eliminate violence against women.
But social media videos showed audience members standing up in the middle of debates brandishing the lion-and-sun flag used by shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, who was ousted by the 1979 Islamic revolution.
They chanted "long live the shah!" and voiced support for his US-based son and Iranian opposition figure Reza Pahlavi.
Read moreReza Pahlavi, son of Iran's deposed shah, positions himself as an alternative to the regime
Monarchists versus left
Among those chanting was Paria Ahmadi, the sister of singer Parastoo Ahmadi, whose flogging for performing without the Islamic hijab sparked international outrage this week.
She took to the stage calling for Pahlavi to return to Iran and declared "long live the shah!"
"Paria stood before France's foreign minister and spoke about the people who had been left out of the conversation," Pahlavi's communications director Tina Ghazimorad wrote on X, complaining the event had only catered to a certain faction.
To display this content from X (Twitter), you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
But Paris-based lawyer Chirinne Ardakani, whose clients include Nobel peace prize winner Narges Mohammadi, said the disruptions were a "serious incident" carried out by "far-right monarchist activists".
She accused the activists of "violence, intimidation and taunting" left-wingers.
To display this content from X (Twitter), you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement.
Film director Sepideh Farsi said the incident was "lamentable" and reflected "what has been going on for a long time within the Iranian diaspora".
The France-based Association Femme Azadi, a pro-monarchist organisation defending Iranian women's rights, alleged left-wing activists were "hijacking the struggle of the Iranian people".
"We will not let anyone steal this revolution from our people," it added.
Divided diaspora
In Tehran, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described the events as a "circus", saying Barrot should "focus on ensuring freedom of expression for Iranians in France before lecturing us about the rights of Iranians in Iran".
But Barrot told France 5 TV that the event was organised "so that Iranian voices can express themselves freely – something they cannot do in today's Iran."
The incident came almost nine months after the killing in a US-Israeli strike on February 28 of supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, sparking the Middle East war.
The millions-strong Iranian diaspora has long been notorious for its internal divisions and spending more time fighting among themselves than the clerics in Iran.
For French academic Clement Therme, author of a recent book on Iran's future, opposition groups agree "on the need for a change of regime in Iran" but disagree on strategy.
"Is one ready to pay the price of war and ally with foreign powers to have a change of regime or prefer to see it collapse from within?" he told AFP.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

items.text:
Egypt detains driver over Cairo fuel tanker fire that killed 31
Prosecutors order drug tests for the 21-year-old suspect, who says he was overtaking when the crash happened.
Prosecutors in Egypt have ordered the detention of a 21-year-old driver suspected of causing a collision on Wednesday that overturned a fuel tanker on Cairo’s ring road, starting a fire that killed 31 people.
The Public Prosecution announced on Thursday that it had ordered the man to be held pending an investigation, and sent him to the Forensic Medicine Authority for tests to determine whether he had taken drugs.
The tanker burst into flames at about 6:30pm (16:30 GMT) on Wednesday, at the height of the evening rush hour, on an elevated stretch of the ring road in al-Waraq, a densely populated district of Giza on the western edge of the capital. The fire spread to passing traffic and destroyed 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles.
In an earlier statement, prosecutors said the driver told investigators he had been travelling from al-Marg towards al-Haram at 110km/h (68mph), with his father in the car, and was switching lanes to overtake other vehicles when the front left of his car struck the rear right of the tanker.
The man told prosecutors he then lost control and his car veered to the far right of the road. One of the tanker’s tyres burst, the statement said, before the vehicle hit a concrete barrier and overturned. Petrol leaking from the truck caught fire.
Identifying remains
Prosecutors said they identified the driver after inspecting the scene and interviewing witnesses, and had since spoken to all the injured whose condition allowed them to be questioned. Forensic teams are taking DNA samples from victims’ relatives to identify some of the bodies. Relatives posted appeals on Facebook for men who had been on the road and had not been heard from since, the Reuters news agency reported.
The investigation will determine whether the driver bears criminal responsibility.
The Ministry of Health and Population on Thursday put the final toll at 31 dead and 26 injured, up from the 21 injured it had reported on Wednesday. Five of the injured have left hospital. The other 21 are still being treated, including eight transferred to other hospitals for further care. The bodies of the dead are in the custody of prosecutors, the ministry said.
By Thursday morning, traffic was moving again after crews cleared most of the burned wreckage. Salah Ahmed, a microbus driver, told the AP news agency that he had been on the ring road when the tanker caught fire but was held back by traffic, which saved his life.
“It was God’s hellfire on the ring road,” he said. “Why is a truck like this on the ring road at a rush hour? Who gets penalised for this happening?”
A 2018 cabinet decision barred trucks carrying more than four tonnes from the ring road between 6am and midnight, the AFP news agency reported. Prosecutors have not said why the tanker was on the road at the time.
“The tanks were exploding, the tyres were exploding, and there was fire,” Zaghlol al-Me, a local resident who reached the scene shortly after the crash, told Reuters. “We just didn’t know what to do or how to save anyone.”
Government pledges support for victims
The Public Prosecution’s statements are the first official account of how the crash happened. Early reports in local media suggested that a high-voltage cable had fallen in front of the tanker. On Wednesday night, the Ministry of Transport denied issuing any statement to that effect and said the cause was a matter for prosecutors.
The Ministry of Electricity and Renewable Energy said the overhead lines were taut when the fire began and that two circuits tripped only after it started. The ministry’s spokesman, Mansour Abdel Ghani, told the Egyptian Youm7 daily newspaper that the lines had no connection to the crash and melted in the heat. A high-voltage line lay twisted on the ground on Thursday, AP reported.
President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi ordered full medical care for the injured and support for the families of those killed. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly visited the injured on Thursday with Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar and Social Solidarity Minister Maya Morsy. Madbouly said the government, civil society and businesspeople would provide bank investment certificates to give bereaved families a stable income, and replacement vehicles for people whose cars burned.
“We realise that no compensation or money can make up for those we have lost,” Madbouly said.
Egypt’s Ministry of Social Solidarity said on Thursday that people could donate through the InstaPay app to help the injured and the families of those killed. It also opened an account at Nasser Social Bank for donations from businesses and civil society groups. The cabinet said the ministry had received 24 million Egyptian pounds (about $445,000) from seven charities.
Calls for accountability
The crash has renewed questions about road safety in Egypt. The Ministry of Transport says it spent about $37bn on transport between 2014 and 2024, yet 5,829 people were killed on the country’s roads in 2025, up 10.8 percent from the year before, and about 84,000 were injured, according to the state statistics agency, CAPMAS.
Egyptian legislators demanded accountability on Thursday. Mahmoud Samy, an MP, said the government needed to move from “building roads and expanding them to managing their safety professionally”. Abdel Moneim Imam, a politician who chairs the liberal Justice Party, said the cabinet bore full responsibility and should resign.
Amr Moussa, Egypt’s former foreign minister and former secretary-general of the Arab League, also criticised what he described as a deterioration in government oversight.
“Trading accusations and evading responsibility leads to the next disaster,” Moussa said, according to Reuters.
Transport Minister Kamel al-Wazir was appointed in 2019 after a train crash at Cairo’s Ramses station triggered a fire that killed 25 p

For eight years, he’s been a mainstay among European leaders, one who’s snatched victory from the jaws of defeat before but has Pedro Sanchez run out of road this time? Spain's Socialist prime minister dogged by incumbent fatigue and nepotism allegations. Sanchez gambled on turning the rift in his coalition over his country's housing shortage into a referendum on his country's strong growth and calling a snap general election.
The housing crisis, the flip side of that growth with more immigrants brought in to power a services-led economy but while Sanchez has proven an outlier among Europeans for embracing new arrivals, the opposition’s tapped into resentment that boiled over last summer with the spectacular images of migrants and asylum seekers overrunning of the North African enclave of Ceuta. If the polls are correct, it’s now the conservatives' election to lose.
Will their standardbearer Albert Nunez Feijoo govern in a coalition with Vox party leader Santiago Abascal? That would be a first for the Spanish far-right since the Franco dictatorship. More importantly, how has Spain’s electorate evolved under Sanchez? Is there still that fierce left versus right divide that persisted after Franco? We’ll ask about generation gaps, gender gaps and what the largest EU member still run by the left for now wants going forward.

Turkey’s Hakan Fidan “has spoken by phone” with his Georgian counterpart, Maka Botchorishvili, the
items.text:
Turkey’s top diplomat has spoken with his Georgian counterpart after incidents at Besiktas’s Europa League match against Israeli club Hapoel Be’er-Sheva in Batumi, a foreign ministry source confirmed.
Turkey’s Hakan Fidan “has spoken by phone” with his Georgian counterpart, Maka Botchorishvili, the source said, adding: “Officials from the Turkish embassy in Tbilisi and the consulate general in Batumi are at the stadium. All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights.”
Turkey’s football federation strongly condemned what it described as “unacceptable” actions undertaken by Georgian police targeting Besiktas supporters who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during the match.
“We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, behaviour and actions directed at Besiktas supporters inside and outside the stadium before and during the Uefa Europa League match between our representative Besiktas and Hapoel Be’er-Sheva in Georgia,” the federation said in a statement.
In a statement, Besiktas accused the Georgian security forces of using “disproportionate” force against supporters before and during the game. “We strongly condemn the security forces for their use of disproportionate force against our fans,” the club said. “We also extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to all our fans affected by these incidents.”
The fixture was being played in ‌Batumi for ‌safety and security reasons and was suspended by the referee, Morten Krogh, in the 26th minute with the score at 0-0 before being restarted after a 30-minute delay, according to Uefa. Georgian police ‌entered the stands and used pepper spray on Besiktas fans, Turkish outlet NTV reported.
The report added that Turkish fans chanted “down with Israel” and that Besiktas players and the club’s director of football, Onder Ozen, spoke to supporters before play restarted to calm ‌the situation. Earlier, the Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel counterparts, the Turkish state-run Anadolu Agency reported.
The match ended in a 2-1 win for Besiktas, who took the lead in the 75th minute through Junior Olaitan and then doubled their advantage in the last minute of normal time with a goal from Orkun Kokcu. Javon East scored a consolation for Hapoel in the third minute of added time.

items.title: Albania's youth are protesting in Flamingo Revolution, not leaving the country anymore
items.summary:
Albania's youth are protesting, not leaving the country anymore
November 26, 2026
In mid-October, students in the Albanian capital Tirana set a suitcase on fire and threw it into the courtyard of the Education Ministry. Everyone in the country understood the symbolism: According to the 2023 census,
items.text:
Albania's youth are protesting, not leaving the country anymore
November 26, 2026
In mid-October, students in the Albanian capital Tirana set a suitcase on fire and threw it into the courtyard of the Education Ministry. Everyone in the country understood the symbolism: According to the 2023 census, the population of this Western Balkan country shrunk by about 420,000 between 2011 and 2023 — by nearly 15% — primarily because of emigration.
For a generation of young Albanians, this was the response to a system that gave them little voice. But now young people want to stay, and the protesters are saying that the system has to change.
Known as the "Flamingo Revolution," the social movement began in May with demonstrations against a luxury resort in a coastal reserve that US President Donald Trump's daughter Ivanka Trump and her husband Jared Kushner were involved in.
It quickly evolved into broader criticism against corruption, Prime Minister Edi Rama's government and his ruling Socialist Party and the country's entire political class.
Thousands marched almost every evening for four months in protests that were largely peaceful. But on October 13, a student protest escalated and there were clashes with police. Since then, the unrest has continued, with police using tear gas, water cannons and rubber bullets against demonstrators. There have been hundreds of arrests and many injuries, amid damage to public and private property.
'Flamingo revolution' has broad support
The protesters have called for Rama's resignation, a transitional government, electoral reform and fresh elections. The movement, which has no leader, has support from people across the political spectrum. And while the prime minister has blamed "foreign hands" for the movement, there seems to be little evidence that external actors are orchestrating the protests, though they may have attempted to exploit the unrest online.
The protesters, who do not feel represented by Albania's democracy, are driven by domestic issues: corruption, the high cost of living and low wages. This is nothing new, but many factors have converged recently: a series of high-level corruption charges, including against ministers and two of Rama's former deputies, rising prices and the fact that Albania is being measured against EU standards by a new generation.
In certain areas, Rama has transformed Albania since taking office in 2013: the economy has grown significantly, as the government likes to point out, and tourism is booming. But the prosperity remains unevenly distributed. Critics accuse the government of channeling too much taxpayer money into a small number of well-connected companies through prestigious projects and public-private partnerships, and in some cases through corrupt business deals, at the expense of healthcare, education and better economic prospects for the wider population.
Rama has rejected the calls for his resignation and has invited protesters to engage in dialogue, which they have so far refused.
Alternating between Socialist and Democratic Party
In 2008, Rama and Sali Berisha, the long-time chairman of the opposition Democratic Party, worked on a reform to Albania's constitution and electoral law, which was approved by parliament. Since then, it is party leaders who have determined who enters Parliament, which weakens ties between lawmakers and their constituents.
In addition, it has become significantly more difficult for new parties to win seats. In 2025, a new party received about 64,000 votes, but only one seat. The Socialists, by contrast, won about one seat for every 10,000 votes.
Rama has been the leader of the Socialists since 2005, while Berisha first became the chairman of the Democratic Party in 1991. For 21 years, Albania's prime minister has either been Rama or Berisha. Freedom House, a US nongovernmental organization that promotes democracy worldwide, classifies Albania as "partly free" and describes the country's political parties as being "often organized around leading personalities."
Protesters on the streets have said that they want both men to be jailed. Rama has argued that governments should be replaced at the ballot box, not on the streets.
Though the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) acknowledged that parliamentary elections in 2025 were "competitive and professionally managed" it said that they had taken place "in a highly polarized environment and contestants did not enjoy a level playing field."
It added that there were "reports of intimidation, misuse of public resources and pressure on public employees, which undermined equal opportunities."
The Democratic Party also spoke of election fraud and intimidation. Turnout was below 45%.
Protesters call out corruption, face high cost of living
Many protesters also allege that when it comes to business, what matters is the proximity to people in power. They criticize the public procurement, public auctions and concessions system, which has led to state-owned land, including coastal and protected areas, being sold to private investors.
Ordinary Albanians are feeling the financial brunt. According to the Albanian Institute of Statistics (INSTAT), half of all employees earn less than 60,000 lek (roughly €620 or $680) per month after taxes. But according to Eurostat, food prices are slightly above the EU average and real estate prices in Tirana have nearly doubled since 2018, with rents rising just as quickly.
For many years, young Albanians who were dissatisfied with the system opted to leave the country. The number of Albanian citizens in Germany more than doubled between 2018 and 2024, reaching almost 120,000.
Though it is still too early to say whether there are fewer Albanians leaving today, for many protesters staying has become a political statement.
Albanians largely pro-EU
Rama has argued that his resignation would jeopardize Albania's bid to join the European Union by 2030, but the vast majority of Albanians are pro-Europea

French actor Gerard Depardieu failed in his attempt to overturn an order for him to stand trial on rape charges.
On Thursday, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that Depardieu should face trial for the alleged rape
items.text:
Gerard Depardieu to stand trial in France for rape and sexual assault
November 26, 2026
French actor Gerard Depardieu failed in his attempt to overturn an order for him to stand trial on rape charges.
On Thursday, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that Depardieu should face trial for the alleged rape and sexual assault that occurred on August 7, 2018. However, the court dismissed the allegations relating to a second incident that occurred six days later.
Depardieu still has the option of appealing to a higher court. His lawyer, Delphine Meillet, told the Associated Press that she disputes Thursday's ruling, though she did not specify whether she will challenge it in France's highest civil and criminal court.
This decision comes just two weeks after the 77-year-old Depardieu dropped his appeal against a sexual assault conviction in a separate case. He accepted an 18-month suspended prison sentence and issued a public apology.
What are the charges against Depardieu?
An actress, who was 22 years old at the time, accused Depardieu of raping and sexually assaulting her at his Paris apartment on August 7 and 13, 2018. Depardieu was 69 at the time of the alleged incident.
She reported the allegations to the police a few days later. Depardieu denies the allegations, claiming that the encounter was consensual.
Last year, a trial was ordered regarding the allegations. If the trial goes ahead, Depardieu could face up to 20 years in prison.
Carine Durrieu Diebolt, the victim's lawyer, said that the Thursday decision was a genuine relief and a victory for her client.
Accusations overshadow Depardieu's legacy
Depardieu was born in 1948 into a working-class family in Chateauroux, a city in central France. He overcame a speech impediment to become one of France's most prolific actors.
The film star was a dominant figure in French cinema for half a century, becoming a renowned cultural export. He earned an Oscar nomination for "Cyrano de Bergerac" and a Golden Globe for "Green Card."
Accusations of sexual misconduct and his subsequent conviction, however, have increasingly overshadowed his cinematic legacy.
The international media has also been paying attention to Depardieu's off-screen antics. One of the most notable instances was when he accepted a Russian passport from President Vladimir Putin in 2013 amid a dispute over French taxes.

items.summary:
Attack on Saudi’s Jazan refinery kills one person, disrupts operations
The attack killed a Nepali national, injured several people and sparked a fire, Saudi Energy Ministry says.
An aerial projectile has hit an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s city of Jazan, killing one worker and injuring several oth
items.text:
Attack on Saudi’s Jazan refinery kills one person, disrupts operations
The attack killed a Nepali national, injured several people and sparked a fire, Saudi Energy Ministry says.
An aerial projectile has hit an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s city of Jazan, killing one worker and injuring several other people, according to the country’s Ministry of Energy.
Thursday’s attack on the facility on the kingdom’s Red Sea coast caused a fire and temporarily halted some operations, the ministry said.
The statement did not identify who carried out the strike, but earlier the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said that the Iranian-backed group had attacked the refinery. It came after Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency had issued an alert about potential danger in Jazan province.
The strike was the Houthis‘ latest blow against key Saudi facilities, a day after the group claimed attacks on Ras Tanura, the kingdom’s largest refinery and a major crude export hub, and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, amid escalating hostilities between the two sides.
The Saudi Ministry of Energy said the worker who died was Nepali, while the injured were of various nationalities.
The injured received medical care, while emergency personnel and specialised technical teams arrived at the site to assess the damage and verify the safety of the facilities following the attack, the ministry added.
The refinery in southwestern Saudi Arabia, near the Yemeni border, is designed to process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day.
The Saudi-led coalition, which is backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its fight with the Houthis, condemned the strike and threatened a counterattack.
“Targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure would be met with a firm military ‌‌response,” coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki posted on X.
Later on Thursday, the coalition claimed its forces had destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launch platform in Yemen’s Hodeidah governorate used by the armed group to stage the attack on the Jazan refinery, according to al-Maliki. There was no immediate statement from the Houthis regarding the strike.
Fighting in Yemen
On the ground in Yemen, meanwhile, Saudi-backed government forces claimed they had carried out 767 strikes on Houthi positions on Thursday.
In a post on X, the forces’ spokesman Majed Abdullah al-Nuzaili said the strikes had “neutralised” 117 Houthi fighters and destroyed 87 vehicles and combat assets.
Al-Nuzaili added that government forces continued to confront Houthi formations on the front lines in northern and western Marib governorate, as well as in the governorates of al-Jawf, Taiz, Lahj, Shabwah and Hajjah.
Earlier on Thursday, a series of air strikes targeted Yemen’s Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, according to media affiliated with the armed group, which is also known as Ansar Allah – Arabic for Supporters of God.
Elsewhere, Houthi forces targeted Habib al-Sarm and al-Hujalla, as well as al-Aqroud in al-Masrakh district.
The Houthis, who control the most populous areas of Yemen, have launched missiles and drones at Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings since the country’s civil war reignited in July, in a spillover from the US-Iran war.
The attacks have previously temporarily disrupted some of Aramco’s operations and caused the cancellation of most international flights to Riyadh. They also forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including football’s AFC Asian Cup and the flagship FII investment conference.
The fighting has also exacerbated dire humanitarian conditions for Yemeni civilians.
The World Health Organization (WHO) reported that as of Monday, 2,361 people had been killed and 10,982 injured since fighting in Yemen escalated in August. More than 360,000 people have also been forced to flee their homes in Yemen since the start of August, according to the UN.

It is the
items.text:
Mexico seeks US talks about suspected SpaceX debris
Mexico concerned as SpaceX ramps up rocket launches from Starbase near border in Texas.
The Mexican government is seeking talks with aviation authorities in the United States about falling rocket debris following SpaceX launches in Texas.
It is the latest sign of growing tensions between Mexico City and Elon Musk’s trillion-dollar company.
“What we are seeking, through the embassy, is a meeting between US and Mexican airspace authorities so that permission for the use of Mexican airspace can be established, how often it would be used, and, if necessary, the relocation of the launch site,” Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Thursday at a news conference in the capital.
“And then there’s the issue of the debris,” she added.
Earlier this month, Mexican authorities said they had to recover debris after a launch of a SpaceX Starship from its Starbase,Texas, facility near the Gulf of Mexico and nature reserves on both sides of the shared border.
Debris that officials said came from the launch washed ashore along Playa Bagdad in Matamoros in the Mexican state of Tamaulipas, according to PROFEPA, Mexico’s Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection.
It said it had collected material several days after part of the Starship was destroyed and fell into the sea. The debris was taken by the Mexican navy to be stored and PROFEPA said it would ask SpaceX to take possession of it.
SpaceX said it was working with Mexican authorities and disputed the claim that what was found was from its failed Starship launch.
“We continue to stay in contact with the Mexican government and are on standby to send support if authorities in Mexico tell us it is actually needed,” the company posted on X. “Partners on the ground relayed that they have found very little debris in their sweeps of the beach and the small amount they have found is not clearly from SpaceX operations.”
Musk’s SpaceX is seeking permission from the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to dramatically increase activity at the Starbase facility. Previously, the company was allowed 25 launches and 50 landings a year, but now it is seeking permission for 456 launches and 912 landings annually.
Earlier this week, the US Federal Communications Commission granted SpaceX permission to send up to one million satellites into space as part of Musk’s plans to develop data centres in orbit.

items.text:
New Zealand vs India: Tom Latham laughs off Rishabh Pant dominating local Christchurch cricket match under false name
Footage emerged this week of India's Rishabh Pant scoring 54 off 21 balls for local Christchurch cricket club Open House Swingers under false name 'Stan Stan'; Pant played one day before second New Zealand vs India Test begins; Black Caps captain Tom Latham laughs it off as 'brilliant'
Thursday 26 November 2026 21:06, UK
New Zealand captain Tom Latham has laughed off India's Rishabh Pant dominating a local Christchurch cricket match under a false name, a day before their second Test.
On Monday, Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips held firm for 43 overs to earn the Black Caps a hard-fought draw in Wellington after India posted a record score of 720-9d.
Pant scored 128 in that Test, with the second Test between the sides beginning on Thursday at Hagley Oval.
Yet, footage has since emerged of Pant playing for club side Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones on Wednesday, scoring 54 off 21 balls under the name 'Stan Stan' to seal a 16-run victory.
In an interview with The New Zealand Herald, Open House player Mohammad Safi said he had seen Pant on an electric bike in the city and asked if he would play, due to his club team being a player short.
"Did he play?! How'd he go?" Latham said at his New Zealand press conference. "That's brilliant!
"It's great. He's obviously a real character of the game, is Rishabh.
"It's great for him to be giving his experience back to LMS (Last Man Standing) teams!"
Pant has scored 3,853 runs in his 53 Tests for India, averaging just below of 45.
The 29-year-old also boasts a strike-rate of 74.43, which is bettered only by Virender Sehwag and Kapil Dev among players to have scored more than 2,000 Test runs for India.
