With Nextcloud Hub 26 Summer, we announced the release of the Nextcloud Office Desktop app powered by Euro-Office. Today, the ready-to-use version
items.text:
On June 9, 2026, we released the first production-ready version of Euro-Office, a sovereign collaborative office suite developed and governed in Europe. With Nextcloud Hub 26 Summer, we announced the release of the Nextcloud Office Desktop app powered by Euro-Office. Today, the ready-to-use version of the app is available for download. It lets you work offline, switch between Nextcloud Hub in your browser and the app on your computer, and get the same experience on Windows, macOS and Linux.
In this article, you’ll learn about the app’s features, how to install it on Windows, macOS and Linux, and how to co-edit files with your team through Nextcloud Hub.
Free desktop office with maximum file compatibility
The Nextcloud Office Desktop app is a free and open source office suite for Windows, macOS and Linux. Featuring editors for text documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and PDFs, it offers high compatibility with Microsoft Office formats (DOCX, XLSX, PPTX) and open formats (ODT, ODS, ODP). Connect it to Nextcloud Hub to edit files with your team in real time.
The app includes the features of Nextcloud Office in your browser, plus the benefits of working on your computer:
- Work offline and keep files on your device
- Use the fonts installed on your computer
- Sign documents digitally
Work with local and online files
With the Nextcloud Office Desktop app, you can edit files locally without an internet connection. Working locally, you keep access to your files and you can keep working when you don’t have internet connection or your online tools go down. You decide which files stay on your computer and which go to the cloud.
Need to access your online files? You can connect your Nextcloud instance to the Nextcloud Office Desktop app to access all the files available to you, and edit them on your own or with your team in real time.
How to connect the Nextcloud Office Desktop app to the cloud:
- Click “+” in the “Clouds” section in the Home tab
- Choose “Nextcloud“ and specify the URL of your instance
- Log in with your credentials
Once connected, choose your Nextcloud instance from the list. You can connect more than one instance to one app to have access to multiple cloud working environments.
Use your own fonts
The Nextcloud Office Desktop app uses fonts installed on your machine, including corporate fonts and default fonts from your OS, like Microsoft fonts on Windows. You can install additional custom fonts any time. No need to bother your Nextcloud admins!
Note: if your collaborators don’t have the same font, they’ll see a fallback font in their version of the file.
Digital signatures and file protection
The Nextcloud Office Desktop app lets you use digital signatures to sign your documents, spreadsheets and presentations. A signature shows who signed a file and that nobody has changed it since. Go to Protection tab and add a signature via Signature feature.
Keep in mind that you need a digital certificate to sign documents. To obtain one, you can ask your IT team at work, or get one for personal use from a trusted provider. You can find providers approved in the EU in this list.
In the Protection tab, you can also set a password for a file, or limit what others can do: comment, fill in forms, or edit with tracked changes only.
How to install the Euro-Office desktop app
You can find and download the latest version of the Nextcloud Office Desktop app from our official installation page.
The app is available for:
- Windows: x64, ARM64
- Linux: .deb (Debian, Ubuntu), .rpm (Fedora)
- macOS (Apple Silicon)
You can also find unsigned builds of Euro-Office desktop app and build the app from the source yourself by following the instructions on GitHub.
We want to keep improving the app. You are welcome to share any issues you find with our engineering team on GitHub.
Want to contribute to Euro-Office? Here’s how to get involved
Contributions are welcome! Whether it’s a bug report, a feature idea, a translation, or a pull request, here’s how to take part:
- Found a bug or have an idea? Open an issue and describe what you ran into or what you’d like to see.
- Want to contribute code? Fork the relevant component repo, make your change, and open a pull request. For build changes, see the build docs.
- Want to help translate? Localization improvements are always appreciated — see the editors’ interface translations.
Please keep contributions compatible with the project’s AGPL v3 license.

Fifa has confirmed it has been the victim of a cyber attack which resulted in personal and business information being stolen.
However, BBC Sport understands the data breach did not include any documents relating to the controversial Fifa
items.text:
Fifa confirms internal data stolen in cyber attack
- Published
Fifa has confirmed it has been the victim of a cyber attack which resulted in personal and business information being stolen.
However, BBC Sport understands the data breach did not include any documents relating to the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.
Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt was this week granted access to the files upon condition of signing a non-disclosure agreement.
It is understood not to be a systems or technology failure at the world football governing body, with criminals able to gain access to the documents by impersonating and taking advantage of staff.
"Fifa can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyber-attack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information," Fifa said in a statement.
"Fifa is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.
"Fifa condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data.
"Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned."
Responsibility has been claimed online by a group called the Handsome Boy Hacking Club, which last week posted screenshots of Fifa files.
The group claims to have gained access to 12GB of data. Analysis indicates this is less than 0.1% of all data held by Fifa and was targeted at the company rather than individuals.

items.title: Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
items.summary:
Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
- Published
Uganda is set to receive its first supplies of a cheaper version of a ground-breaking injection to prevent HIV, raising hopes of expanding access to the drug across Africa, where the burden of the disease remains highest.
The
items.text:
Hope for millions as cheaper HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
- Published
Uganda is set to receive its first supplies of a cheaper version of a ground-breaking injection to prevent HIV, raising hopes of expanding access to the drug across Africa, where the burden of the disease remains highest.
The first global shipment of the generic drug, known as lenacapavir, arrived in Zambia on Wednesday, with deliveries to Uganda expected in the coming days, the Global Fund has said.
The drug, administered as an injection twice a year, is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection and is expected to cost just $40 (£30) per person annually.
Zimbabwe is due to receive supplies early next year, with several other countries expected to follow.
The arrival of the generic drug comes just a year after the original version, developed by US pharmaceutical giant Gilead Sciences, became available in sub-Saharan Africa.
The original version cost about about $28,000 annually in the US, putting it beyond the reach of many of those in developing countries.
Lenacapavir works by targeting the protective protein shell of HIV, disrupting the virus's ability to multiply and establish an infection in the body.
In a landmark clinical trial involving more than 5,000 adolescent girls and young women in Uganda and South Africa in 2024, none of those who received the injection contracted HIV.
Health experts say the injection offers a major advantage over existing HIV prevention pills, known as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which must be taken every day and can carry social stigma.
The World Health Organization (WHO) recommended the drug for HIV prevention in July 2025.
The Global Fund described the arrival of the drug in Africa as a "major breakthrough" in the fight against HIV, saying cheaper supplies would help reach millions more people at risk of infection.
"These deliveries mark an unprecedented acceleration and expansion in access to a highly effective, quality-assured generic HIV prevention medicine in low- and middle-income settings," the group said in a statement on Wednesday.
More than 189,000 people across 10 countries have already received their first injection of lenacapavir, according to the Global Fund.
The organisation expects 24 countries to have received supplies by the end of this year and, working with the US government, plans to reach at least three million people by the end of 2028.
It is eventually expected to be available in 120 low- and middle-income countries.
Sub-Saharan Africa accounts for nearly two-thirds of people living with HIV globally, with adolescent girls and young women disproportionately affected.
South Africa has the world's largest HIV-positive population, with nearly eight million people living with the virus. It is among the countries expected to receive the cheaper injection.
Some 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV last year, while 570,000 died from HIV-related illnesses, according to the WHO.
The rollout comes amid concerns that sweeping cuts to US foreign aid under President Donald Trump's administration could undermine decades of progress in tackling HIV in Africa, where many countries rely heavily on international funding for prevention and treatment.
The UN aims to end Aids as a public health threat by 2030.

items.title: ‘We are on the edge’: how Swedish league declined from summit of women’s game
items.summary:
On 12 October 2003, Sweden stood still. The women’s football team were playing Germany in the World Cup final. TV4 set a new viewing record as almost half the nation watched the game go into extra time, where Nia Künzer scored the golden goal winner after 98 minutes.
It was a bitter pill to swallow
items.text:
On 12 October 2003, Sweden stood still. The women’s football team were playing Germany in the World Cup final. TV4 set a new viewing record as almost half the nation watched the game go into extra time, where Nia Künzer scored the golden goal winner after 98 minutes.
It was a bitter pill to swallow but there was still the belief that the tournament would mark the start of women’s football’s commercial breakthrough in Sweden. After all, how could sponsors and broadcasters ignore such undeniable interest?
It was not only the national team who were flying high. A few months earlier Umeå had won the equivalent of the Women’s Champions League (then called the Uefa Women’s Cup) and would do so again the following season. The best players in the world came to play in Sweden, including Marta, but despite the success and growing crowds sponsors were conspicuous by their absence and pay remained low.
A decade later Tyresö reached the Champions League final with future world champions such as Christen Press, Meghan Klingenberg and Whitney Engen in the squad. But crippling debts forced the club out of the top flight. In fact they went from a Champions League final to bankruptcy within a month.
New sponsors needed
This summer, the Swedish wonderkid Felicia Schröder moved from Häcken to Real Madrid for what the Gothenburg club said was a world record fee (which would have meant more than £1.1m). According to Fifa’s latest report, no women’s league in the world received more in transfer fees during the summer window than the Damallsvenskan. It is easy to believe the league is thriving.
But what many had long feared has now become reality: both the main sponsor and the title sponsor are ending their partnerships with the Damallsvenskan. In addition, at the time of writing, the top flight still has no TV deal for next season. How can such a good product be so hard to sell?
Malmö FF’s Australia international Amy Sayer knows the league well, having told her agency that playing in Sweden was her top priority coming out of college in 2023. She joined the standalone club Kristianstads DFF (who are not affiliated to a men’s side) and then Malmö, who have had a strong men’s team for a long time but whose women’s side were founded in 2019.
“I get a lot of questions about Damallsvenskan and for players who want a bigger challenge and a way into Europe, it’s a league I’d highly recommend,” she says. “But I think we are on the edge. The league can turn it around, but as players we are worried that it’s not going to grow.”
Where are the fans?
Traditionally, the league has been built on standalone women’s clubs. But a few years ago, Sweden’s biggest men’s clubs experienced a kind of collective awakening. They saw the commercial potential in investing in women’s teams, looked enviously at Arsenal Women’s growing attendances and let their imaginations run wild.
But the belief that supporters would flock to women’s matches has proved to be a huge misjudgment. The average attendance record from the Umeå era in the early 2000s, 1,127, still stands and this season the figure dropped below 800 per match.
Sayer had expected bigger crowds when she joined Malmö. “It really surprised me,” she says. “We have great communications staff and we share an Instagram account with the men’s team. But something is holding back the lifelong supporters.
“At my old club [Kristianstad] it was about a family feeling and building a sense of unity. But we were always chasing funding. At a standalone club there’s always that feeling: will we survive next year?”
A divided league
Looking for explanations, some point to poor media coverage, others to the league operator’s lack of resources. Some blame the 51% rule, which requires Swedish clubs to be majority-owned by their members. Yet the rule did not stop Rosengård, the league’s most decorated club, from selling 47% of its women’s team to the British investment firm Crux. Instead of the hoped-for boost, the deal cost the club its most loyal supporters, who walked away in protest with a banner reading: “Goodbye! Better a B-team than a business.”
Less than an hour from Sayer’s former club lies Vittsjö. The small village has around 1,800 inhabitants, yet its club has spent 15 consecutive seasons in the top flight. After finishing an impressive sixth, the club posted an image on social media: “We need your help”, alongside a bank account number.
Many placed their faith in the affiliated clubs, with their deeper pockets and large fanbases, to finally become the league’s saviours. However, the anticipated surge has failed to materialise, increasing questions about the league’s future.
And nowhere were those questions more visible than in last week’s play-off for a place in the Damallsvenskan. KIF Örebro faced Rosengård over two legs even though the tax authorities had issued them with a winding up petition. They then became the first second-tier side ever to win the play-off, only to file for bankruptcy themselves on Wednesday. Now Rosengård, the league’s most decorated club, look set to keep their place in the top flight. It remains to be seen whether the investors at Crux and the high-profile football director, Caroline Seger, can lead the club out of its crisis.
Interest in Swedish women’s football has never been the problem, but turning it into engagement with the Damallsvenskan clearly has. Now the league must be repackaged in a way that reflects the different realities of its club models, with supporters at its heart. As Sayer says: “Women’s football is so exciting. It’s so creative – what the players can do is incredible. But I think a new culture has to be built.”
The answers simply will not come from sponsors or broadcasters, but from the people who actually turn up. And none of this necessarily starts with money. It starts with a genuine dialogue.

items.title: Neville, Carragher and the inescapable podcasting feedback loop of doom | Jonathan Liew
items.summary:

items.text:
A podcast studio in Manchester. A production runner pours water into jugs. Gary Neville enters the room with Michael Carrick.
Neville: Just so you know, we’re already filming. This is the intro bit, where we show everyone coming on to set and doing some light banter. It humanises us. The viewer sees it and thinks we’re just mates chatting about football, rather than scions of a global podcast empire commercially obliged to produce an endless scroll of provocative content for money. I always say: why can’t you be both?
Carrick: OK, so …
Neville: Hang on, these Huel bottles need to be showing the label. Who’s turned the Huels round? Pathetic.
Jamie Carragher enters, followed by Roy Keane and Jill Scott.
Carragher: Salford failed to win at the weekend, Gary!
Neville: Yes, but banal observation about young James at Wigan!
Carragher: AHAHAHAHA!
Neville: AHAHAHAHAHA!
Ian Wright enters, humming a Mary J Blige tune.
Neville: You’re watching Stick To Man United on The Overkill, with ManBank. Look, we all know there are times when you just want to bank with your mates, in a room, together. Download the ManBank app today. We’ve got a special guest today: the former manager of Manchester United Football Club, Michael Carrick. Now Carra, before we start …
Carragher: Which Carra? Me or him?
Neville: AHAHAHAHA!
Carragher: AHAHAHAHAHA!
Neville: The situation at United right now, it really hurts. I say that as a fan, I don’t use this word lightly, but it’s a real tragedy what’s happened to this football club. OK, you’ve got Grimsby and MK Dons. You’ve got the relegation in 1974. You’ve got Tommy Docherty leaving the club in disgrace. You’ve got Old Trafford being destroyed in a bombing raid during the second world war. You’ve got the very real threat of bankruptcy in the early 1900s. This, to me, is worse than any of that.
Carragher gazing at the ceiling: I always think about the great United teams under Sir Alex. Vidic. Ferdinand. Jaap Stam. Wes Brown. Patrice Evra. Even Denis Irwin, going back to Bruce and Pallister. You had Schmeichel in goal. You had Ince and Bryan Robson in midfield. You had Mark Hughes. You had Cantona. I look at the current side and think: do I see a Mark Hughes in there? Do I see a Cantona? And the answer is: only to an extent.
Neville: Roy, how do United move forward from this? They’ve got Brentford at the weekend.
Keane shrugging: Well, a team like Manchester United, you should always be beating a team like Brentford.
Neville: Yeah, but how do they go about it?
Keane: Well, the players in that dressing room, they need to be looking at themselves. And saying: come on, a team like Manchester United should always be beating a team like Brentford.
Neville: But tactically, what’s the plan?
Keane: If you keep asking me the same question, you’ll get the same answer, only louder.
Scott: I remember something Sarina was telling us at the Euros. We’d just beaten Norway and …
Neville: You take a look at that defence. Yoro. Mazraoui. Dalot. De Ligt. You can’t tell me there’s a worse defence in the history of professional football than those four. You put those four up in a park game, and it would be carnage. You choose any four inanimate objects – say a Kleenex, a butternut squash, a roof tile and a Belkin USB-C to Lightning charging cable – and they would do a better job in defence for Manchester United Football Club.
Carragher: Only thing making it worse is if you and Phil were playing in it!
Neville: AHAHAHA!
Carragher: AHAHAHAHAHA!
Wright: Look, I see this United team now, which Roy played in, and Gary played in, and I just think: where’s the heart? Where’s the soul? It’s like they’ve lost something. And until they get it back … I don’t know. I just can’t feel it. I’m not feeling it.
Keane: But you talk about heart, and you talk about soul. These are international footballers! It’s their job! I’m inexplicably furious about this point in particular!
Carragher: Let’s bring Michael into the discussion here, because you were dealt a tough hand, not just in terms of the recruitment, but the level of scrutiny around the club, around any big club, there’s a noise there. I remember talking to Daniel Agger about it. And Martin Skrtel. Steven Gerrard. Xabi Alonso. Dirk Kuyt.
Scott: There is that constant background chatter, though, isn’t there, at a club like United? I remember Sarina once telling us …
Neville: I remember, the gaffer – Sir Alex – once telling us that at United, a defeat is a disaster. Because of that constant background chatter. Because of how it would be perceived in the media. Did you feel like that constant judgment, whether it was from the media, or from fans, or from prominent ex-players, sometimes on podcasts: did you feel like that was creating extra problems for you?
Twenty-second ad for Manbrella, a precision-engineered umbrella made specifically to fit the male palm. Press Skip to return to video.
Neville: Did you feel like those ex-players in the media, players who had won trophies at United, but who now earn a living off talking about the club, almost preferred it when the club was failing? Because it gave them something to talk about? Because it made their own era look rosy in comparison? Because it did better numbers? And did that broader need to manufacture crisis, to paint every setback as if it was the worst disgrace in human history rather than the inevitable variance of a transitional team in a strong league labouring under an absentee ownership, create an inevitable doom spiral, an inescapable feedback loop from which even the very best managers have struggled to escape over the last 13 years?
Carrick: Well …
Carragher: Sounds like you could be talking about yourself there, Gary!
Neville: AHAHAHA!
All: AHAHAHAHAHAHA!

items.title: ‘Not Bayern-like’: Joshua Kimmich fumes at club’s treatment of Jamal Musiala
items.summary:
The Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club’s “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.
Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala’s performances and contract after repeated seizures ca
items.text:
The Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club’s “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.
Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala’s performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in pre-season games, drawing protests from the players’ union Fifpro. Now Kimmich, the club’s vice captain, has spoken out and warned Bayern risked undermining their family image.
“What I don’t understand is the way this is being communicated in public,” Kimmich said after Bayern’s 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday. “It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it’s not bigger than a person. That’s an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either.”
Kimmich also suggested Musiala’s run of injuries over the past two years, including a badly fractured leg at the Club World Cup last year, may have had more impact on his game than the neurological condition.
“It’s not the case that he has problems because he’s unprofessional,” Kimmich said. “He’s there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself.”
Bayern met with Musiala’s agents on Tuesday and clarified the timeline of events, dismissing speculation Musiala could have concealed the condition when he signed his last contract extension. Bayern said the club and Musiala’s representatives accepted he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after the contract extension.
“This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared,” Bayern said.
Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing in pre-season games, leaving players and fans alarmed.
Bayern’s head coach, Vincent Kompany, said at the time the incidents were triggered by a change in the medication Musiala was taking. Musiala was rested for the start of the season and has since missed several games with a muscle issue.
Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Bayern’s loss at Lille, which capped a bad week for the club. Harry Kane injured his ankle on Friday and faces months on the sidelines. Bayern have also lost the lead in the Bundesliga and slipped to 15th in the Champions League standings.

items.title: Intel One Mono font
items.summary:

Identifying the typographically underserved low-vision developer audience, Frere
items.text:
Introducing Intel One Mono, an expressive monospaced font family that’s built with clarity, legibility, and the needs of developers in mind.
It’s easier to read, and available for free, with an open-source font license.
Identifying the typographically underserved low-vision developer audience, Frere-Jones Type designed the Intel One Mono typeface in partnership with the Intel Brand Team and VMLY&R, for maximum legibility to address developers' fatigue and eyestrain and reduce coding errors. A panel of low-vision and legally blind developers provided feedback at each stage of design.
Intel One Mono also covers a wide range of over 200 languages using the Latin script. The Intel One Mono fonts are provided in four weights — Light, Regular, Medium, and Bold — with matching italics, and we are happy to share both an official release of fonts ready to use as well as editable sources.
To install the fonts, please use the provided builds under Releases. Please refer to your software’s documentation for how to activate and use these fonts.
- VSCode - In Settings, search Font Family, then specify Intel One Mono
- Sublime Text - Go to Sublime Text -> Preferences -> Settings and set font_face to Intel One Mono
- IntelliJ Platform - Go to File -> Settings -> Editor -> Font and set Font to Intel One Mono
- We recommend the .otf or .ttf format for desktop use.
- The .ttf files are also well suited for mobile apps.
- The .woff and .woff2 fonts are optimized for web use.
We recommend using these fonts at 7 points and larger in print, 9 pixels and larger on screen. The .ttf, .woff and .woff2 fonts provided in the official release have been manually optimized for screen display, improving clarity and legibility, especially on Windows platforms.
Outside of the default characters, there are a few extra features that are accessible in some applications, as well as via CSS:
- Programming Ligatures: To use programming ligatures, activate the ss01 feature (Stylistic Set #1). Additional refinements are available via ss02 and ss03: Stylistic Set #2 switches the <= and >= combinations to arrow forms (math contractions being the default otherwise), and Stylistic Set #3 additionally activates a “www” ligature.
- Alternate three: New in release 1.5. Alternate form for three added. The round top three, numerator, denomenator, superior and inferior can be activated with stylistic Set #4.
- Raised Colon: The colon is automatically raised in operators, to align with math symbols. For non-programming contexts, the raised colon can be applied contextually between numbers or activated generally. The contextual option is available via ss11 (Stylistic Set #11); for the global switch use ss12 (Stylistic Set #12) or salt (Stylistic Alternates).
- Language Support: ccmp and locl features ensure correct display across a wide range of languages. These are usually active by default. We recommend setting the language tag/setting in your software to the desired language for best results.
- Superior/superscript and inferior/subscript figures are included via their Unicode codepoints, or you can produce them from the default figures via the sups (Superscript) and subs/sinf (Subscript) features.
- Fraction numerals are similarly available via the numr (Numerator) and dnom (Denominator) features. A set of premade fractions is also available in the fonts.
Programming ligatures are not active by default. To use them, activate the stylistic sets of your preference in your code editor. For example:
- VSCode - In Settings, add "editor.fontLigatures": "'ss01'"
- Sublime Text - In Settings, add "font_options": ["ss01"]
You will find editable sources in the sources directory. The instances subfolder contains separate source files for each style of the typeface. Sources are provided in .ufo files, which contain complete artwork, links to OpenType features provided in separate .fea files, as well as meta information like naming and vertical alignments for each style of the typeface.
These are not installable fonts, but rather the source files that produce them: UFO (Unified Font Object) is an open, human-readable font source file format; you can find the file spec here. These sources were created using RoboFont. Many other font editors will also be able to open .ufo files; we recommend using RoboFont version 4.4.
For instances, you will find postscript and truetype subfolders; these contain separate source files for the .otf format and the .ttf/.woff/.woff2 files respectively. Since the format for the outline drawings differs between these sets of formats, for best results we recommend using the postscript sources to create .otf fonts, and the TrueType sources to create .ttf, .woff, or .woff2 fonts.
After making your desired edits, you can generate installable fonts directly from the font editor using its “Generate Font” functionality. If you use RoboFont, any install options should default to the ideal settings, but here they are for reference:
- For .otf builds, we recommend activating “Decompose” as well as “Autohint” options.
- For .ttf, .woff and .woff2 builds, we recommend activating the “Autohint” option only (see note on hinting below).
- In any case, we recommend using the “Release Mode” setting for best results.
If you would like to apply edits across multiple weights, a more advanced yet potentially efficient way is to edit the masters. These are special sources that describe the extreme points in the design space — the lightest and heaviest weights for both roman and italic designs.
After editing masters, you will need to rerun interpolation to generate individual weights and styles within that design space. This requires the .designspace files enclosed with the masters. The designspace format is an open, XML-based format that describes interpolation spaces (format specification for reference). For a RoboFont-based workflow we recommend Skateboard for interpolation; you can also use the free DesignSpaceEditor extension to view and edit

items.title: Delap's chance at redemption against toothless Chelsea
items.summary:
Liam Delap has a chance to show Chelsea what they're missing when they travel to Nottingham Forest
Liam Delap has a chance to show former club Chelsea what they are missing as Xabi Alonso's side continue to struggle in attack without Joao Pedro; watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports
items.text:
Liam Delap has a chance to show Chelsea what they're missing when they travel to Nottingham Forest
Liam Delap has a chance to show former club Chelsea what they are missing as Xabi Alonso's side continue to struggle in attack without Joao Pedro; watch Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea live on Sky Sports Premier League and Main Event on Friday Night Football; kick-off 8pm
Wednesday 25 November 2026 12:17, UK
When Liam Delap joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he probably had ambitions of cementing himself as an elite Premier League No 9. Perhaps even positioning himself to be the heir to Harry Kane's throne for England.
Less than a month later, Joao Pedro made the move to Stamford Bridge and suddenly, the landscape changed. He was not the first-choice striker at the club.
What followed was an arduous campaign that brought three goals in 47 games and saw Delap succumb to what is now the fabled curse of the Chelsea No 9 shirt.
A club-record move to Nottingham Forest in August has yet to truly revitalise his career either. But Oliver Glasner does have faith that there's a 20-goal-a-season striker hiding in the 23-year-old. What better time to showcase it than against his former employer?
This isn't just an opportunity for Delap to prove a point, mind. If anything, this game comes at the most opportune time to show Xabi Alonso exactly what he is missing at this very moment.
- Sky Sports' new Premier League predictor!
- Transfer Centre LIVE! | Forest news & transfers🔴⚪
- Forest fixtures & scores | FREE Forest highlights▶️
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- No Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract📺
Since Joao Pedro has been on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Chelsea's devastating attack has often looked tame. Without the Brazilian as a focal point, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer have struggled to hit the same heights. As Paul Merson playfully put it: "if you had The Three Musketeers but took one of them out, you'd struggle to sell a film."
Joao Pedro has not played since the 2-0 win on October 17 against Everton. In the four Premier League matches since, Chelsea have lost three and won once against 10-man Manchester United. In those games, they scored three goals. They managed more than that in wins over Bournemouth and Brighton prior alone.
Alonso has tried all sorts to combat the loss. They played without a recognised striker against Tottenham and got ripped apart. The same approach was used in the defeat to Sunderland. Against United, Willian Estevao tended to operate centrally while Emmanuel Emegha was finally given the chance against Leeds. He scored but also had the fewest touches of any starter that day, being the only one to remain in single digits.
Danny Welbeck would appear to be the most obvious option, but Alonso appears reluctant to use his very own Benjamin Button from the off. That makes Emegha the only natural choice.
It's difficult to compare Delap and Emegha from last term for different reasons. The former was often watching from the bench while the latter was out from December to April with injury at Strasbourg. The season before, though, indicates that perhaps Delap could offer a little more with his all-round game.
What makes Joao Pedro so unique to Chelsea is not purely his scoring numbers. It is the fact that he is a consistent top-10 performer among all Premier League strikers with his link-up play.
While Emegha's data shows him to be more prolific in front of goal, the Englishman is far closer to Joao Pedro in build-up play than his Dutch counterpart. There is still a gulf in quality as you'd expect, but it certainly shows that the former Ipswich man was probably more suited to filling in when the Brazilian is unavailable.
That was the case two seasons ago and is even more so since he has joined Forest. The indication being that even in a period that hasn't been so fruitful, he has still been able to develop.
Delap has shown he can thrive when he has a chip on his shoulder. His brace against Manchester City was as great an example as you could find to show that. Against another former club, with his team struggling to get results and fans fans beginning to grow frustrated.
That was the night he announced himself to the City Ground faithful. On Friday, it will be an opportunity to announce himself to the travelling supporters, something he'd have wished to have done by this time last year.
He may even be further buoyed by the fact that his former side are struggling just as much at the back as they are in attack. Chelsea have the fifth-worst defensive record in the Premier League from the first 11 games.
That is a mouth-watering fact for any striker, let alone one who has no excuse but to have the bit between his teeth. It feels as though the cards have fallen as perfectly as they possibly could for Delap to have his say.
No one will ever know if there's a scenario where Delap staying could have been beneficial for his career. But Friday Night Football is his platform show it would have been beneficial for the Blues.

items.title: Collins: I got choked up before I came on for my Wales debut!
items.summary:
Aaron Collins exclusive: MK Dons striker discusses electric start to 2026/27 and first senior Wales call-up
Aaron Collins discusses making his senior Wales debut and his incredible start to the season; the 29-year-old has scored 17 goals in 17 games for MK Dons so far in 2026/27; watch MK Dons vs No
items.text:
Aaron Collins exclusive: MK Dons striker discusses electric start to 2026/27 and first senior Wales call-up
Aaron Collins discusses making his senior Wales debut and his incredible start to the season; the 29-year-old has scored 17 goals in 17 games for MK Dons so far in 2026/27; watch MK Dons vs Notts County live on Sky Sports+ on Saturday; kick-off 12.30pm
Wednesday 25 November 2026 14:24, UK
On Friday November 6, Aaron Collins was notified by the FAW that he was on the standby list for Wales' Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal.
He knew it was a step in the right direction, but his form - 17 goals and three assists in 16 games in all competitions at the time - seemed more than worthy of an official call-up.
A first chance for the MK Dons striker to represent his country since an U19 friendly defeat to Germany in April 2015 was tantalisingly close, yet just out of reach.
Until November 10, that was.
- Got Sky? Watch EFL games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream EFL games with no contract📺
Wrexham's Kieffer Moore withdrew from Craig Bellamy's squad and Collins was called up to take his place.
"That was a call I've been waiting for for a long time," Collins tells Sky Sports.
"I don't score goals to be like: 'I'm going to get called up now', because I know the level I'm at, and I've got to prove a lot to get that chance.
"But after being a pro for 12 years, I did think the older I was getting, the less chance I was going to get. Of course that crossed my mind.
"It was a shock to finally receive the call and know I was going to represent my country at international level."
In Oslo, Collins was an unused substitute as Wales suffered a 3-1 defeat to Erling Haaland, Martin Odegaard and co.
Hearing 'Land of My Fathers' for the first time stirred something inside.
"It really choked me up. I grew up watching the rugby team and the football team singing it and you get goosebumps then. But to be able to stand there and sing that national anthem as a proud Welshman, as one of the players, was something that I would have never even thought I'd be able to do."
Back in Cardiff against Portugal, Bellamy told him at half-time to make sure he was ready to go if called upon.
After 63 minutes, he came on alongside Brennan Johnson to make his senior debut.
"I got choked up again then!" Collins says.
"To actually be able to achieve that and have the honour of having a Welsh badge on my chest entering the pitch was just crazy.
"I enjoyed it and I just played with no fear, like I had nothing to lose. I did what the manager wanted from me; I didn't manage to get any real chances, but you're at the elite level and it's not going to be as easy."
Having not played against Norway, he did not go searching for a shirt swap "out of respect for the lads who played".
But against Portugal "I was walking down the tunnel I saw Diogo Dalot and I got myself a shirt to treasure along with my debut shirt".
Those two shirts are not the only new additions to the room where Collins puts his accolades on display.
In the last league game he played before his Wales adventure, on October 31, he scored four in MK Dons' 6-1 demolition of Doncaster.
That mammoth effort earned him another match ball for the collection - the second of the season and fourth of his career - as well as the Compare the Market Goal Hero of the Month award.
"I'd never scored four in a game before - that's a new achievement ticked off!"
"The only thing I can put my form down to is confidence. Any attacker knows that when you're in your flow, you're in your flow, and when you're scoring and assisting, there's that feeling where you feel like you're not going to miss.
"I'm in hot form and I do expect everything that I hit to go in. It's a feeling I need to cherish and try and make last as long as possible."
Collins' hot streak comes after a turbulent 2025/26 season, during which he helped Paul Warne's side to promotion from Sky Bet League Two, but suffered three significant injuries that greatly reduced his playing time after a reported £800,000 move from Bolton.
That misfortune is fuelling him.
"Coming into this season, I had this different kind of hunger to make up for last season where I came in as, maybe you could say the marquee signing, and didn't really get to live up to that," he adds.
"Being fit and ready to kick on - and to start of the season the way I have - has been a real achievement. Now I can show why I've been signed, and hopefully fans can go, 'Aaron Collins was a good signing!'
"To get to 17 in 17 games is a huge achievement so far, and there's plenty more games to come. My goal is to get to that 20 mark as early as possible, and even get to that 20 mark in the league as early as possible, and carry on kicking on."
If Collins carries on in this fashion, he might be a shoo-in for another Wales call-up in March.
Created by Compare the Market, in partnership with the EFL, the Goal Hero of the Month award celebrates the most memorable and impactful goals from across the Championship, League One and League Two.
It aims to shine a spotlight on the stories behind them and what they mean to the clubs, players and supporters involved.

items.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
items.summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off “the private chat histories of more
items.text:
A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to prevent Character.AI from selling off user data as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. In a deluge of nearly identical press releases, the various AGs accuse the company of planning to auction off “the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts — more than 2.1 million of them registered to minors — with no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold.”
42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
A bipartisan coalition of AGs say Character.AI is planning to sell the personal data of minors to the highest bidder.
In October, Character.AI filed for bankruptcy following years of scandals and legal challenges, including from Disney. Disney ended up buying some of the company’s assets and hiring its CEO, Karandeep Anand, in a sort of “acquihire” arrangement that will also see “a number of Character.AI’s technical team” join the entertainment giant. The Disney deal also faced opposition from a similarly broad coalition of AGs.
The main point of contention with Character.AI’s plan to sell its chat data is that it offers no protections for users. The AGs say there are no requirements that the buyer honor existing privacy policies, no avenues for users to delete their data, and no inherent limits on what a buyer could do with that data, including selling it on to yet another party. It doesn’t help that the first bidder has a limited paper trail, having only been established on November 13th, 2026, with no parent company or investors listed.
Some states, including New York, Connecticut, California, and Colorado, have also passed laws regulating chatbots that Character.AI may be in violation of when they go into effect on January 1st, 2027.

items.text:
Mauricio Pochettino claimed Manchester United were punished unfairly after again appearing to suffer from faulty officiating in Wednesday night’s 2-2 draw at Sporting.
The key decision from Szymon Marciniak came when Amad Diallo’s first-half strike was ruled out due to the referee adjudging Youri Tielemans to have fouled Gonçalo Inácio just before the finish. Tielemans was booked and so when he received a second yellow card in second-half added time, he was sent off for United’s fifth red card in their last nine games. This followed Leny Yoro’s red card in Sunday’s 4-0 loss at Liverpool that was later rescinded.
“It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished [so much] in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions,” said Pochettino, who greeted questions about the official’s first caution of Tielemans by saying: “It’s difficult to understand why that happened on the field. Impossible.”
With 10 minutes left United were 2-1 ahead but suffered a chaotic ending as Senne Lammens dropped a high cross in front of his goal, allowing Luis Suárez to equalise with a bicycle kick.
Pochettino defended his No 1. “Football is about making mistakes,” the head coach said. “I want to support always my player. It’s something that happened in that case. We need to talk about responsibility and it’s our responsibility too to provide the best tools.
“In this type of action also our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult. It’s not to blame the defensive line, but it’s two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on. Because sometimes we talk about that professional players need to have refreshed concepts, details until that becomes a habit. And things that we need to improve are habits in a defensive way, offensive way, in all the areas.
“But of course, we need to accept, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve, you know, the small details that for sure we will improve.” Lammens saved a first-half penalty from Suárez before conceding another one himself moments later, which the striker converted.
Joshua Zirkzee also offered support to Lammens. “This team is a family, so there’s no one who will suffer by themselves,” the striker said. “Mistakes happen. Let’s go on to the next one. Senne’s a great goalkeeper. In this moment, we just give him space … We all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game. And we didn’t draw because of him. I’m also someone who likes to look at myself and, you know, I didn’t score.”
Zirkzee refused to blame Marciniak for the outcome. “Our team should be capable to win even if we’re not being favoured in those moments,” he said of certain refereeing decisions. “We’re in a place where it can feel like [everything is against United] pretty quick. But we’ve got a locker room that’s built on supporting each other and we will get out of it eventually. And if it’s us against the world, so be it.”
Bruno Fernandes equalised from the spot on 48 minutes before his bizarre long-range effort – which took a huge deflection off a divot in the pitch – put United ahead.
Despite the chaotic end, Pochettino was impressed by his team. “The structure was really good,” he said. “All the microdoses that we add to the team, I think is helping the structure to be very clear.”

Oliver Bearman has signed a one-year contract extension to remain with Haas for the 2027 F1 season; watch the Qatar GP on Sky Sports F1 this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday
Thursday 26 November 2026 09:09, UK
Haas have confirmed Oliver Bearman will stay at the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season, after protracted contract talks resulted in a one-year extension.
Despite both the British driver and American-owned team having repeatedly insisted they wanted to continue together, negotiations had dragged on for several months, leading to speculation that his ties to Ferrari - who he remains tied to after coming through their academy - were a factor in the delay.
The 21-year-old said ahead of last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix that he was "disappointed" a resolution had not been found, but the wait for confirmation was finally ended by Haas on Thursday ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix.

"It's no secret that I'm delighted to be continuing with TGR Haas F1 Team into 2027," Bearman said. "This team has played an integral role in my development, and I've felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here.
"We've got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I'm excited to lead that work, building on what we've achieved, and striving for even more together - we have unfinished business."
Bearman completes Haas' 2027 line-up, with Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara having last month been confirmed as Esteban Ocon's replacement.
Ocon was meant to see out the 2026 season but a fall out between the Frenchman and the team saw him replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa in Mexico, before Camara was given the final four races of the season to prepare for his full debut campaign.
Confirmation of Bearman's new deal also completes the 2027 Formula grid, with all 11 teams having now confirmed both of their drivers for next year.
Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us.
"We've seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward."

items.summary: Simon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a
items.text:
Simon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a permanent fixture in the Premier League over the past 14 years. Palace finally secured a major trophy in the 2025 FA Cup final – an experience Teesdale remembers as “one of the best days of my life” – and followed that up by winning the Conference League but he decided in August not to renew his season ticket.
“Something happened between the FA Cup win and today that changed me,” he wrote in an emotional article published last month on his website. “Tipped me over the edge. Actually, it’s fairer to say that something accelerated in that period of time. The seeds were sown years ago.”
Teesdale details how the matchday experience at Palace – bottom of the Premier League for the first time since 2017 after five straight defeats – has been transformed by “fireworks, light shows and excessively loud music at key moments before, during and after the match”. He likens it to listening to Natasha Bedingfield’s Unwritten – one of the most unpopular songs on the Palace playlist – on a loop. “A song about writing your own story, that’s played on matchdays to drown us out as we attempt to write ours.”
“As a fan of another team, people will be thinking: ‘What on earth are you moaning about?’” Teesdale says. “But it’s harder to put your emotions and your experience of what it’s like to commit to being a fan into words that are beyond just what you see on paper, like winning trophies and whatever else. If I had to tie it down to one thing, it was the perception that the club was losing its identity. It just seemed that no one was really being thought about as a genuine Palace fan any more.”
Teesdale’s decision to give up his season ticket happened to coincide with the news that Palace’s influential supporters’ group the Holmesdale Fanatics (HF) was disbanding 24 hours before their first home game of the season against Manchester City.
In February, it had criticised the club’s attempts “to keep trying to force an ‘American-style experience’ on us” after asking for the music to be turned off during the warm-up, only for that request to be refused by Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, blaming Uefa regulations. The HF claimed another request to turn off the music before a Premier League game against Leeds a few weeks later was rejected because the club had a “production plan” in place for matches.
The HF’s statement in August cited “never-ending problems with the club right up to the present day” as one of the reasons for its sudden disappearance from its traditional home behind the goal in Block E of the Holmesdale Road Stand. “Attempts to sanitise the game are stronger than ever,” it wrote.
The HF’s absence has been felt significantly at Selhurst Park. Pierre Sage said early in his doomed 16-game spell as manager that the unique atmosphere it created at home and on the way to the Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano had played a part in convincing him to succeed Oliver Glasner. “We are waiting for them, I expect they will come back quickly,” he said in September after the 4-0 win over Lech Poznan.
The Palace chair, Steve Parish, defended the pre-match playlist and told the Athletic in an interview a week later that he was disappointed by the HF’s decision to disband but remained confident that “something exciting will grow out of it”. Teesdale was also contacted by Lacey after his article was published last month and she told him that she expected them back, “in a slightly different format”, in Block E soon. When approached by the Guardian, a former member of the HF did not want to comment and referred to its August statement announcing it would end all organised stadium activity at Selhurst Park after 20 years.
A defamation claim lodged in the high court by the Nottingham Forest owner, Evangelos Marinakis, 16 days before the announcement the HF was disbanding could be another explanation for their continued absence.
It was made a fortnight before the one-year limitation period was due to expire against Palace’s owners, CPFC Limited, and “Persons Unknown” in response to the incendiary banner held up in the Holmesdale Road End during Palace’s game against Forest in August 2025. Marinakis says that it made a number of serious allegations about him and depicted him holding a gun to the head of the England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White. The case is due to be heard in the coming months, with Marinakis and CPFC Limited having instructed prominent solicitors and “Persons Unknown” to be represented by “litigant in person”, ie themselves.
Palace were fined £50,000 by the Football Association after being found guilty of failing “to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) didn’t behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, insulting and/or provocative way at this match”. The FA added in its statement in February: “The fact that Crystal Palace had a policy to prevent banners being smuggled into the stadium demonstrates that it was aware of the risk.”
Parish and Lacey have said publicly they did not know exactly why the HF – whose motto was “this mentality is unstoppable” – disbanded and there was no mention of the banner on its statement. Yet it seems extremely likely there is a connection.
Teesdale says he was surprised to receive a call from Lacey but believes the only female chief executive in the Premier League has Palace’s best interests at heart. It is understood there are plans for some supporters to bring a drum to Thursday’s Europa League meeting with Real Sociedad in an attempt to fill the void for Thomas Frank’s first home game in charge. Teesdale is still deciding whether to attend.

Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah on Wednesday announced
items.text:
Guinea orders residents to clean up the capital months after deadly rubbish dump collapse
- Published
Guinea has ordered residents to do a mass clean-up of the capital, Conakry, months after a rubbish landfill collapsed, killing dozens of people.
Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah on Wednesday announced a deadline of 31 December to clear rubbish in the city and its suburbs, which has seen an increase in illegal dumping in recent months.
In August heavy rains caused a landslide at the capital's main waste dump, with the rubbish collapsing onto homes killing 31 people and injuring others.
The site in the city's Dar es Salaam area was subsequently closed permanently, which has led to piles of rubbish accumulating outside homes and on the streets.
At a public forum on sanitation, Sanitation Minister Aboubacar Camara said Conakry was generating about 3,000 tonnes of waste every day.
He said much of the garbage was ending up in the streets because of weaknesses in the collection system.
The prime minister called on local authorities to become more involved in organising waste collection, saying this could become a way to create jobs.
"The state will do its part, but the municipalities must also organise themselves to ensure waste collection and provide jobs for young people," the prime minister said.
"Conakry must be completely clean by the end of December," he added, relaying a directive from the country's president, Mamady Doumbouya.
He cited measures the government was taking to improve waste collection and recycling, including a national sanitation fund that would guarantee financing for the sector.
Camara said talks had been finalised with a waste collection operator, with a plan for equipment to move waste from transit and sorting centres to a new disposal site in Baretodé, outside the capital.
The August tragedy at the Dar es Salaam landfill was not the first - 10 people were killed at the same site in 2017.
The government had ordered people living close to the site to move, but many residents chose to stay.
According to the prime minister, the government now plans to transform the closed waste site into an urban park.

items.text:
Why KMI Panel frustrates referees too - and impacts their salary
- Published
It has become something of a Wednesday morning ritual for fans. At 10am, the Premier League releases the latest votes of its Key Match Incidents Panel.
It did not used to be this way.
For four seasons, the KMI Panel was a clandestine operation. It was distributed to clubs only, but it would still find its way out into the public domain.
This season, it began being released to the public.
Yet little is really understood about the KMI Panel.
Why does it exist? Is it just protecting referees? And does it really mean anything?
For referees, the last question is more important than you might realise.
The votes, which ultimately say whether referees have got a decision right or wrong, create a merit table of performance - and this impacts their salary.
"It depends where you are on the list," former Premier League referee Graham Scott said. "But if you're in the middle, then it might be 25% of your take-home. So it's substantial."
For the officials, these are not decisions being taken by their bosses.
Their performance reviews are effectively outsourced to a group of former players.
The results can be inconsistent and frustrating as much for the referees as they are for the fans.
What makes up a Premier League referee's salary?
Let's take a look at how a referee's salary works in the Premier League.
A Premier League official will earn, on average, about £175,000 per year. The scale will run between £125,000 and £250,000.
Think that is unduly high? Referees in Spain's La Liga are the highest paid in the world, according to Marca, with an average yearly salary of £221,000.
Premier League officials are about on par with those in the German Bundesliga and Italian Serie A.
In England, there is a guaranteed base wage of 50%. This will differ depending on the seniority and experience of an official.
Michael Oliver would be at the top of the bracket, a newcomer like Farai Hallam at the other end.
The other 50% is based upon a set of variables, with match fees a major part.
Each on-field appointment is worth a little over £1000, with a VAR game slightly less.
How does this break down in real terms?
Last season, Anthony Taylor refereed the most Premier League games, 31, followed by Chris Kavanagh, 30, and Michael Oliver, 29.
Kavanagh and Oliver worked as VAR on a handful of occasions, while Taylor did not do any.
Stuart Attwell had the most combined appointments at 52, with 25 games as a referee and 27 as a VAR.
Finally, there is the subjective element - the KMI Panel.
The votes determine the annual bonus payments for all officials.
'Ultimately, the KMI Panel lacks any real credibility'
Until 2022, referees' body Pro Ref, or PGMOL as it was known until this summer, used to do its own assessment of its referees' decisions.
But clubs grew restless, feeling referees were marking their own homework.
And so the KMI Panel was born.
It is made up of five members. Three are former players and coaches, plus there is a representative for the Premier League and one for Pro Ref.
Their identities remain secret, with the former professionals selected from a pool on rotation.
What you won't see on the published version is that each incident is given a difficulty rating, ranging from one to five, which is taken into account when drawing up the referees' merit table.
All this really is, of course, is another layer of subjectivity. On top of the referees, VAR, players and coaches.
And it causes frustration.
"People complain about the consistency of referees on field, of VAR interventions, or otherwise," said Scott, who now acts as the refereeing expert for the Athletic.
"But then, if you look at the KMI Panel outcomes, they're also inconsistent."
It is a view shared by Andy Davies, who retired as a Championship referee last year.
"Naturally, there will always be a level of interest given as it provides a significant part of income for the season," Davies said.
"But ultimately, the KMI Panel lacks any real credibility amongst referees."
Split decisions are 'contentious and inconsistent'
Referees are scored on their on-field decision-making. If an error has been corrected by the VAR, it still counts as a mistake for the merit table.
Those at the top of the table will be rewarded well, while those at the bottom are not likely to receive much of a bonus payment at all.
Let's take a look at the numbers from last season.
Michael Oliver was the top referee, getting 93.5% of KMIs correct. John Brooks, Darren England and Simon Hooper were very marginally behind.
For other referees, the borderline decisions, ones which are the most subjective and sit in the grey areas, can be an issue.
One vote could be the difference between a referee being right or wrong. And a place on the merit table, impacting how much they get paid.
Last season, Sam Barrott and Jarred Gillett were both told they made four errors to a 2:3 vote.
Attwell, meanwhile, had three of the more high-profile incidents go in his favour to a 3:2 vote.
"The ones that sit in the margins can be very contentious and inconsistent," said Scott.
"You think, well, how can that be right? You know, that's not definitive, is it? It could have gone either way.
"But there seems to be a reluctance to allow that 'seen them given' sort of mentality, neither right nor wrong.
"Relying on such a small group of people to be so definitive, especially when they vote 3:2, is unhealthy and unhelpful."
'The game can afford to invest more in this process'
As well as determining the merit table for each referee's salary, what the KMI Panel says can guide how games are refereed.
But this causes problems, too.
The members of the KMI Panel can be influenced by public opinion, and inconsistency means referees are often having to change the way they approach games, only to be told it is wrong.

In a series of X posts, Gen Kainerugaba ap
items.text:
DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats
- Published
The Democratic Republic of Congo has summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the president's son.
In a series of X posts, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to support a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo. He insisted that Uganda's military involvement was purely driven by security concerns.
The DR Congo's foreign ministry summoned Uganda's envoy to explain the remarks, describing them as "particularly serious" and damaging to diplomatic relations.
The Ugandan government has yet to respond.
The diplomatic row comes despite close military ties between the neighbours.
Their forces have been conducting joint operations against the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern DR Congo since 2021.
Uganda has also recently been involved in efforts to mediate between the Congolese government and an armed group led by former warlord Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province.
- The Ugandan general who lobs grenades on Twitter 
  - Published30 October 2022
In his posts, Gen Kainerugaba accused the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), an armed group operating in eastern DR Congo, of targeting members of the Bahema ethnic community.
The Bahema are a traditionally cattle-herding community mainly based in DR Congo's north-eastern Ituri province.
They have historical and cultural ties to the Bahima people of neighbouring Uganda.
He also threatened a rebel takeover of Walikale, in North Kivu province, while defending Uganda's military presence in DR Congo.
Walikale is rich in mineral resources , including some of the country's largest tin deposits and several major gold mines.
Gen Kainerugaba's X account, which had nearly 1.4 million followers, has since become inaccessible.
It is unclear whether he deactivated it, as he has done in the past, or whether the platform had suspended it.
During the same week he declared: "My tweets in Uganda are directives that must be obeyed."
The posts followed reports that a DR Congo military aircraft had allegedly been shot down by rebels, with foreign mercenaries reportedly among those on board.
Gen Kainerugaba criticised the reported presence of foreign mercenaries in DR Congo.
"These remarks, which are particularly serious, have caused a major media incident and undermine the necessary restraint that must prevail in relations between sovereign states," the DR Congo foreign ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.
"The Congolese government expects the Republic of Uganda to clarify its official position and take the necessary measures to prevent such transgressions from recurring in the future".
The ministry added that DR Congo remained committed to regional peace and stability but would defend its dignity and institutions against "any form of provocation or interference".
It is not the first time Gen Kainerugaba's social media posts have strained relations between the two countries.
In February last year, he threatened to seize the eastern DR Congo city of Bunia, claiming that members of the Bahima ethnic community were being attacked.
In 2024, DR Congo also summoned Uganda's diplomatic representative after the general made threats against foreign mercenaries operating in eastern DR Congo.
The 52-year-old general, widely seen as a potential successor to his father Yoweri Museveni, has become known for his provocative social media posts.
In 2022, he sparked a diplomatic row with neighbouring Kenya after threatening to invade the country and capture its capital, Nairobi, prompting his father to apologise forn the remarks.

items.title: ‘I hope they win Ashes 5-0’ – Stokes backs Root and Fleming's new England
items.summary:
Ben Stokes on Sandpapergate, the Ashes, and Joe Root and Stephen Fleming's new era in charge of the England Test team
"I always felt on as England captain. Now I can just be Ben, not Ben Stokes captain of the England cricket team. Looking back, it's not really a healthy place to be at," Stokes told
items.text:
Ben Stokes on Sandpapergate, the Ashes, and Joe Root and Stephen Fleming's new era in charge of the England Test team
"I always felt on as England captain. Now I can just be Ben, not Ben Stokes captain of the England cricket team. Looking back, it's not really a healthy place to be at," Stokes told Sky Sports, adding: "I'm still an England cricket fan. I want the players, Joe and Flem to do well"
Tuesday 24 November 2026 17:09, UK
Former England captain Ben Stokes says he hopes they win next year's Ashes 5-0, though he would not be drawn on Sandpapergate or the possibility of him making a comeback for the series.
Speaking to Sky Sports upon the launch of a new podcast he's presenting with former England team-mate Mark Wood called 'That's Not Cricket', Stokes hinted that he might have more to say on the saga dominating Australian cricket on that platform.
"It would be pretty bizarre for it not to be mentioned [on the podcast]", Stokes said. "It's all kicking off at the moment out there, isn't it?
"What Australia have going on there is far beyond anything we had to deal with [as a leadership group].
"I imagine Joe [Root] and Flem [Stephen Fleming] would be thinking, 'imagine if this happened three weeks before the Ashes next year, as opposed to now'."
'Root and Fleming will work really well together'
England's Test team enter into a new era under Root - who returned to the captaincy with a 3-0 series sweep of Pakistan following Stokes' international retirement - and Fleming, who begins as head coach with a three-Test tour of South Africa next month.
The series, against the reigning World Test Champions, serves as an ideal challenge for the new regime as they steel themselves for the visit of Australia next summer where they'll look to regain the Ashes for the first time since winning on home soil in 2015.
"I'm doing a Glenn McGrath here; I hope England win the Ashes 5-0," Stokes said. "I'm not saying they will, but I wish nothing but the best for them.
"I'm still an England cricket fan. I want the players, Joe and Flem to do well.
"There is no animosity whatsoever between any of us, there's no jealousy."
Stokes did add, however, that he was "surprised" to see Root take on the captaincy again, knowing first-hand how much the job takes out of you - as well as the toll it had taken on Root by the time he handed over the reins in 2022 after five years in the role.
"I was a little bit surprised, if I'm being honest, just because he knows what it's like and he's done so well as a player but also, knowing Joe, he feels like he can take the team from where it was and build on it again," Stokes said.
"It's an exciting time for someone to think like that and when Stephen Fleming got appointed, I thought 'these two are going to work really well together'.
"I did a lot of work with Flem in the IPL. He's a great man manager; everyone has already seen how he speaks, which is very impressive. I'm excited to watch them go about it."
Stokes: Everything after Ashes defeat was tough
Stokes' time as Test captain and as an England cricketer came to an end with a 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand, which was on the heels of a disastrous 4-1 Ashes drubbing in Australia during the winter.
"I was in the right headspace for the Ashes," Stokes reflected. "It was all after that. Before the Ashes, I was so confident.
"Everyone was fit, firing and ready to go. Fans and pundits were all confident, and Australia weren't confident, so we couldn't have been in a better place going out there.
"But emotion and the feeling of what you think is going to happen is completely different to getting out there in the heat of the battle. Everything after that was tough."
Stokes added: "Unfortunately, to do that role, you have to immerse yourself in it, have to throw yourself into it.
"For all the positive stuff that comes with it, there is a negative effect that can flow over into your home life and your family.
"I think every England captain will have that. I don't think there is anything you can do.
"You can try your hardest, but when you do that role you just have to do it. I don't think you are doing the role justice if you take it lightly.
"I always felt on as England captain. Now I can just be Ben, not Ben Stokes captain of the England cricket team. Looking back, it's not really a healthy place to be at."
As well as still playing for his county side Durham - helping them clinch promotion back to Division One of the County Championship - and an upcoming stint with the Adelaide Strikers in the Big Bash League, Stokes is using his newfound freedom to venture into the world of podcasting.
"I have been in the public eye for so long but people who don't know me probably only know 10, 15, 20 per cent of what I am actually like," he said. "That is the exciting thing: I now get a chance to say what I want to be going out.
"I don't feel like you're always necessarily able to give that full account of yourself as a person, because you're wary of upsetting people. The only person I can upset now is myself.
"It's really exciting and I can't wait to get going. We've got a lot to talk about and a lot to say."

items.text:
'Laughing gas has ended careers' - so how common is it in football?
- Published
It is known as laughing gas but the impact nitrous oxide can have on a professional footballer's body is anything but funny.
"I'm not going to name names but I have colleagues who know Premier League footballers who are no longer playing as a direct result of nitrous oxide [use]," said Dr David Nicholl.
Nicholl, a clinical lead in neurology with Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust, was speaking after former Manchester City, Chelsea, Liverpool and England forward Raheem Sterling was handed a suspended jail term after pleading guilty to dangerous driving.
A key part of the case was that Sterling had been inhaling nitrous oxide from a balloon while driving.
His Lamborghini was seen veering across a motorway and later crashed into a metal gate. Sterling, 31, was arrested at the scene and found with six gas canisters in his car.
He disclosed to custody staff "he had a problem with nitrous oxide", the court was told.
Defending Sterling, Jason Bartfeld KC said his client "recognised the various unhealthy coping mechanisms that brought him to this position" and that he has "sought to address" these in the "most positive and effective way and with some success".
So, what is nitrous oxide, how does it affect those who take it and is its use more common in footballers than the wider population?
What is nitrous oxide?
Nitrous oxide's original use was as a sedative that healthcare providers like dentists could use to keep patients comfortable during procedures.
It is now legally sold for catering, medical and industrial purposes, but is frequently used as a recreational drug and is commonly known as laughing gas.
This can be abused by inhaling the gas via a balloon, leading to a short-term high causing symptoms such as brief euphoria, mild perceptual changes and uncontrollable laughter, external.
Nitrous oxide also slows brain and body responses and can displace oxygen in the lungs and bloodstream, contributing to dizziness, confusion or fainting.
It is thought long-term or excessive use can have disastrous effects on the body, from neurological harms to nerve and spinal cord damage which could lead to permanent disability.
According to medical journal The Lancet, it is now the third most commonly used drug after cannabis and cocaine in the UK, with use highest among people aged 16–24 years.
It has been increasing in popularity as a recreational drug over the past decade.
This prompted it to be reclassified as a Class C drug in 2023 after a government consultation.
Is it widely used by footballers?
BBC Sport has been told the abuse of so-called laughing gas has been widespread among professional footballers for a long time.
Former player Drewe Broughton is now a human performance coach, working with Premier League footballers and clubs around the world.
He said laughing gas was seen by some as a release.
"I think the use of nitrous oxide is really common," he added.
"It's something that can be done in private. It's something that can be hidden. You can't smell it on their clothes or the breath. It's an underground thing."
Broughton said he had been in the company of professional players when they had been using 'balloons'.
"I remember sitting in a players' house on the outskirts of Manchester, and these canisters were all over the floor," he added.
"I was from a world where people drank or they gambled or went to pubs and nightclubs. That was my first exposure to it."
Broughton has developed an app to help tackle issues with mental health and under-performance in football.
He said the reasons to use nitrous oxide had always been there: pressure on players to perform leaves them searching for an escape.
But Broughton has concerns about the toll nitrous oxide can take.
"I don't think there's the same awareness around nitrous oxide and damage to the body as there would be around alcohol or other drugs," he said.
BBC Sport has been told that some footballers see laughing gas as an alternative to harder substances because it does not stay in the body's system for more than a few hours.
Luci Hanmer, who works with Lancashire drugs and alcohol support charity 'We Are With You', said a substance like nitrous oxide was hard to detect.
She said: "Anything that you're inhaling, the effects that you're going to feel happen very soon.
"So if you are looking for that escapism, the effects are going to be quick.
"Once ingested, it doesn't last very long within your body compared to some of the other substances which can be detected for quite a number of days.
"So if you're getting a drugs test the next day for example, that won't show up."
- Sterling given suspended sentence for dangerous driving 
  - Published17 hours ago
'The worst thing you want to be using as a sportsperson'
Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha said more support was needed, particularly for players like Sterling who break through young.
Sterling made his debut for Liverpool and England at just 17 - before going on to win four Premier League titles at Manchester City and 82 caps for his country, including the Euro 2020 final at Wembley.
"Look at what's happened to Raheem," he said. "Look at how this led to this moment, a moment which I'm sure he's hugely embarrassed about, because I'm sure he can see how dangerous that was to not just his life, but the lives of so many people who are on the road at the same time.
"But I just don't feel like football is in a position where they think it's important to support people who have issues with nitrous oxide."
The BBC Radio 5 live pundit said the use of nitrous oxide in professional footballing circles was very common.
"I think the difference from when I was younger is that people would openly party in certain places," he said.
"Now they party where they're harder to spot. That's why you don't really see on a week-to-week basis now the scandal of somebody that's been out drinking.
"The players are doing it, but it'
